  fleetSubtypes, so a CharacterCard (not in cardTypes=[FLEET]) always returned
  false from `allowsCardType`, entering the alongside-fleet check. If a fleet
  was alongside, the check passed, but then execution fell through to the
  trailing `if (!part.allowsCardType(c)) return false;` which re-rejected the
  character. Fix: (1) changed the leadersIncluded guard from
  `!part.allowsCardType(c)` to `!part.getCardTypes().contains(c.getType())` ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â
  tests ONLY cardTypes membership, not fleet subtypes; (2) changed the trailing
  check from `if` to `else if` so a character that passes the alongside-fleet
  check is NOT re-rejected by the standard cardTypes filter.

* **War-conflict participation bug fixed**: `Conflict.canJoinConflict` had an
  erroneous `initiatorRace.isPlayableBy(playerRace)` check in the war-conflict
  branch beyond the `isAtWar` check. War conflict participation is gated solely
  by the TensionMatrix warfare state, not by card playability (which governs which
  player can play cards of a given faction). Removed the `isPlayableBy` clause.

* **testWarConflict() implemented**: B5-0376 Phase A war-conflict test method
  (14 assertions covering initiation, participation, and card commitment) was
  referenced but missing in HeadlessConformanceTest.main(). Implemented and
  uncommented in main(). All 14 WAR checks pass.

* B5-0397 superseded ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â its target failure is fixed by the canCommitCard change above.

The watcher breaks its poll on `roundNumber > 1` (HeadlessSmokeTest.java:134-137) while the daemon loop continues round 2; step 5 (HeadlessSmokeTest.java:195-224) then calls `chooseAction` on live state. * Decision: no game-logic defect exists to fix. The B5-0505 slice should extend the step-5 checker exemption to all non-hand payload types (harness fixture) or quiesce the loop at a phase boundary before step 5; seeded RNG alone (0482 precedent) cannot close the window because the nondeterminism is thread scheduling, not RNG.

## 2026-09-27 ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â opencode (space-bunny-free): CORRECTION to the B5-0613 close-out and its pattern record

[CORRECTION 2026-09-27, opencode (space-bunny-free): the B5-0613 close-out reported a verified fix and filed a reusable lesson; independent execution shows the lesson is wrong on three counts and the underlying stop-condition defect was NOT fixed. The B5-0613 code change and report are left byte-intact; this entry is the correction. Per supersede-never-rewrite the defective pattern record is not edited ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â a correcting record is filed at `.agent/PATTERNS/opencode (space-bunny-free)/2026-09-27-correction-the-runner-regex-mandates-a-tautological-self-check.md`.]

* **What B5-0613 got right.** The tolerant leading-pipe anchor is a real fix: the old single-pipe pattern matched 301 ledger lines, the tolerant pattern matches 312, with no duplicate IDs extracted. Row *visibility* improved.
* **Error 1 ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â the shipped self-check is a tautology and cannot fail.** It counted matches using the *same* pattern that built the row list, so it compared a set against itself. It reported `312 == 312` as acceptance evidence while 9 rows carried a corrupt status and 4 rows were invisible. The lesson filed alongside generalises this into a rule with a *must* ("self-check that returned-row count equals the count of lines matching its own filter pattern ... so a row filter defect reports itself"), which is the harmful form: it propagates a dead check as a mandate.
* **Error 2 ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â the ID pattern still cannot see letter-suffixed task IDs.** The lesson prescribes `^B5-\d+$`, and `\d+` does not match the trailing letter of `B5-0202c`, `B5-0329a`, `B5-0330a`, `B5-0331a`. Those four rows remained invisible to the tool after the fix. Correct form is `^B5-[0-9]{4}[a-z]?$`. All four are finished rows, which is why no claimable task was hidden and nobody noticed.
* **Error 3 ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â `Status`, the field the stop condition actually reads, was never addressed.** This is the load-bearing omission. The runner's stop condition is `Get-LedgerRows | Where-Object { $_.Status -eq 'OPEN' }` (line 117), and `Status` was still assigned from the hard-coded `$parts[2]`. On a `||`-prefixed row the split yields `['','',' B5-0604 ',' OPEN ']`, so `$parts[2]` **is the ID**, and those rows can never satisfy `-eq 'OPEN'`. The lesson does not mention `Status` at all, which is why it reads as complete when it is not.
* **Measured consequence.** After the B5-0613 fix the tool reported **17** OPEN rows while the ledger held **24**. Invisible: `B5-0572`, `B5-0574`, `B5-0604`, `B5-0605`, `B5-0606`, `B5-0607`, `B5-0608`. Had those been the last unclaimed tasks, the runner would have printed "Queue drained: no OPEN task without a live claim. Done." with 7 claimable rows on disk. **This is the exact false negative that caused six waves of unnecessary hand-seeding.** The human was not confused and the reporting agents were not careless; the tool was returning a confident wrong answer, which is more dangerous than failing because it is believed.
* **Fix applied.** `.agent/run-queue.ps1` `Get-LedgerRows` now derives both `Id` and `Status` by scanning split cells for the first value matching the expected shape, so neither depends on a positional index; the ID pattern is widened to `B5-[0-9]{4}[a-z]?`; the self-check compares against a deliberately permissive, separately written pattern (`^\|+\s*B5-[0-9]{4}[a-z]?\s*\|`, no capture group, no ID constraint) plus a distinct warning for any row parsed with no recognisable status. PowerShell only, no Java touched, `b5ccg/` unchanged.
* **Verified.** Runner OPEN **24 == 24** disk OPEN; 0 OPEN rows invisible to the filter; 0 rows parsed without a status; 316 rows with 0 duplicate IDs; all four suffixed IDs resolved (`B5-0202c=DONE`, `B5-0330a=DONE`, `B5-0331a=DONE`, `B5-0329a=DONE`). Method: the parser was extracted and exercised in isolation, never by invoking the runner.
* **Disclosure ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â a mistake in my own verification.** I first tested by dot-sourcing with `-WhatIf`. The script declares no such parameter, so PowerShell ignored it and the main loop executed: it printed "Claiming lane for B5-0574" and launched a `freebuff` agent, which died on command-argument parsing. Verified benign ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â no `B5-0574.json` claim file persisted, row `B5-0574` text unmodified, no work performed. Four `node` processes were left running because they are most likely other agents' live sessions.
* **Standing guidance added.** A self-check must compare its subject against something independently derived, never against its own predicate; the test before shipping one is *what input makes this red?* ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â if the answer is "none" it is a comment, and shipping it as evidence is worse than shipping nothing. And a parser fix and a **consumer** fix are separate tasks: fixing row visibility while the consumer filters on row status yields a tool worse than broken, because it returns wrong answers instead of omitting rows. A query-tool fix is not done until the consumer's own filter has been re-run and reconciled against ground truth by hand.
* **Left undone, disclosed.** B5-0613's own row remains `|| B5-0613 | DONE |`, a non-canonical leading double pipe; it is visible to the corrected parser but the delimiter is still wrong, and B5-0611's named band is 0604-0608 so 0613 is an unowned instance. B5-0613 scope items 2-5 remain unseeded, most importantly `Test-LiveClaim` liveness via heartbeat and report mtime with `UNKNOWN` on an absent signal, which is what would stop a reaper killing live work.
* Reusable lesson: a self-check that reuses its subject's pattern is not weak evidence, it is *no* evidence ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â and a false lesson filed in the pattern store is worse than no lesson, because the store is boot-skimmed and the next agent will implement the mandate and quote the green result as proof. Filed as `2026-09-27-correction-the-runner-regex-mandates-a-tautological-self-check.md`.

* B5-0624, on human order to fix the `run-queue.ps1` letter-suffix crash second. LATENT, not live, and the distinction is the task: `[int]` on a stripped task id throws for the `B5-nnnnX` class at two sites, the `Sort-Object` key over claimable rows and the lane-assignment site, so any OPEN suffixed row takes the whole runner down rather than failing one task. Every case in the first suite asserted `crash=False` and not one asserted the VALUE of the key, so green tests checking only the absence of the original symptom will happily pass a replacement that is worse. A crash announces itself; a silently degenerate key does not. The B5-0624 suite therefore asserts the picked task ID, which is what caught it. Checking the approved text against the repo rather than trusting it found TWO STALE STATEMENTS IN THE PROMPT ITSELF, both of the same species this repo keeps recording, namely a pointer adjacent to a citation that was never checked against it: (1) the prompt cited the pattern skim as step 10, but B5-0614 inserted the census step and renumbered 5 through 11 to 6 through 11, so it is step 11 and the prompt predated that repair; (2) the prompt stopped when "the ledger is empty", which never happens, since the ledger accumulates and 322 closed rows is a healthy ledger rather than an empty one, so it now reads "no OPEN row remains". Both were fixed before filing. Both were invisible precisely because the surrounding text was a complete, confident specification, which is the same failure mode as a self-certifying gate: confident and complete is not the same as verified.
* The filed procedure also carries a clause-to-failure table mapping thirteen rules to the recorded incident that made each necessary (B5-0568, B5-0597, B5-0609, B5-0613, B5-0614, B5-0618, B5-0622, B5-0337, Amendment A1.1 among them), on the principle that a procedure clause with no failure behind it is decoration; and a section recording the three ways this loop has lied to itself, being a pre-write id check that races another reader and is therefore insufficient, a fix that removes a symptom by introducing a silently degenerate value per B5-0624, and a validator never observed red, which is not evidence of anything.
* Reusable lesson: a rule you have just written is not evidence that you followed it, since the fragmentation here was created by the agent that authored the rule four files at a time; and a confident, complete specification is not a verified one, because both defects in the approved prompt were invisible exactly where the text read as though it had been checked. ## 2026-09-27 ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â opencode (space-bunny-free): B5-0626 DONE ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â the unattended path now boots from a document that is true

* `HANDOFF.md` is not merely out of date, it is misleading in a way that produces a specific wrong action: its section 7 states `b5ccg/src/` is RED under `-source 6` when it has been green since 2026-09-21, and its section 9 instructs the reader to claim B5-0001, which has been DONE since 2026-09-21. An unattended agent obeying that literally would have created a claim file against a DONE row, which is precisely the orphan class B5-0622 spent a task closing the protocol against. The automated path was about to walk straight into the bug the previous task had just fixed, by following a document nobody had re-read since day one.
* PART 1: the `$TaskPromptTemplate` is repointed at `AGENT_LOOP.md` while KEEPING `00_BOOT.md` as the boot step. Rewriting it surfaced that the template was also missing four rules only the new procedure carries, folded in rather than left as cosmetic tidying: the SANITISED agent-id in the report filename per B5-0623, the reusable-lesson line filed as a NEW file under `.agent/PATTERNS/<agent-id>/` with supersede-never-rewrite, the binding heartbeat schema in `HEARTBEATS/README.md`, and the re-read-the-row-still-OPEN check beside the claim-file check per B5-0622. The template also carried its own stale pointer, `mark BLOCKED per step 7`, when verify is step 8 of the current eleven-step boot file, which is the SECOND instance of exactly this defect in two tasks after B5-0625 found the same class in the human-supplied prompt at `step 10` when it was really 11. A pointer adjacent to a citation is not checked against it, however carefully the surrounding prose was written. One instruction was added at a cost of one line: do NOT read `HANDOFF.md`, because an agent that remembers the old pointer will look for it and being told where not to look is cheaper than hoping it does not.
* PART 2: `HANDOFF.md` is marked superseded in its OWN frontmatter with a machine-readable `superseded_by` block naming boot, loop and reason, its status set to "Superseded (retained for history; not authority)", an `assessor_llm` entry and updated `last_modified` fields added, and a banner placed above the body that NAMES BOTH false statements specifically rather than saying only that the document is old. ## 2026-09-27 ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â opencode (space-bunny-free): B5-0627 DONE ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â the AGENT_LOOP stop clause no longer asks for a commit hash that cannot exist

* B5-0627, on human approval to fix the wording so an agent is not asked for something the loop never does. `.agent/AGENT_LOOP.md` only; no behavioural code touched and no `src/` or `resources/` edit.
* The defect: the STOP condition read "Then report the run: iterations, tasks closed, commit hash, and every file deliberately left uncommitted", which is self-contradictory in a single sentence because it demands a commit hash and a list of uncommitted files in the same breath, as though a run were expected to commit some things and leave others. There is no middle case: the loop commits nothing.
* The claim that no commit hash can exist is a claim about CODE, so it was verified rather than asserted, and the ordering is the point: `git commit` appears in NEITHER `.agent/AGENT_LOOP.md` step 7 NOR the `run-queue.ps1` task template, so the invariant the fix asserts is one the code already had and only the prose contradicted. Changing the wording first and checking the code afterwards would have made the document its own evidence.
* CENSUS BEFORE EDIT, and the thirty left alone: a repo-wide search for the phrase returned THIRTY-ONE occurrences, of which exactly ONE was a live instruction, being this clause, while the other thirty were historical close-out reports and ledger rows recording tasks that genuinely did commit and were correct when written. All thirty were left untouched, because rewriting a historical report so it agrees with present behaviour falsifies the record and a ledger is append-only for a reason. This is the flip side of the B5-0625 lesson about stale pointers: fix the live instruction, leave the archaeology. The temptation to bulk-edit all thirty-one is exactly what would have corrupted the record.
* The replacement states the invariant positively, that the loop does not commit, that neither step 7 nor the runner template has a commit step, that committing and pushing remain human decisions, and that a run ending with a dirty tree is a CORRECT run and not a failed one. That last sentence is the one that earns the edit: without it an agent handed the original wording has two bad options and no good one, being to fabricate a hash or to report the run as broken, and both are worse than reporting honestly. The first is plausible because the instruction is confident, the second because a dirty tree looks like an error to anyone expecting a commit. Stating that a dirty tree is the correct outcome removes the trap rather than merely documenting it.
* Verified by re-reading the file from disk after the edit rather than trusting the editor: no longer asks for a commit hash, now states that the loop does not commit, the surrounding code fence is still balanced, the YAML frontmatter still opens on line 1, the em dash in the new clause is a real U+2014, and no mojibake or double-encoded sequence was written anywhere in the file.
* Reusable lesson: a small fix can still be worth a full close-out, because the reason to file it is not the size of the diff but that the defect was LIVE, and liveness is the only property that makes prose worth correcting. Report: `.agent/REPORTS/2026-09-27-opencode (space-bunny-free)-B5-0627.md`.

## 2026-09-27 ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â opencode (space-bunny-free): B5-0628 DONE ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â the runner could not pass a quoted prompt to any native CLI

* B5-0628 originated from the HUMAN's own failed run rather than a seeded row, and the terminal output supplied the evidence: hermes rejected the tail of the task prompt with "is not a `hermes` command" and exited 2. `.agent/run-queue.ps1` only; no `src/` or `resources/` edit.
* Reading the error before theorising located the cause immediately, because the fragment hermes quoted began right after the phrase `"Reusable lesson"` in the task template. The first hypothesis was WRONG and was killed by reproduction: newlines were suspected, but a two-line prompt containing newlines exited 0 and was understood, proving newlines are safe and are NOT the trigger. The trigger is DOUBLE QUOTES. Had the fix collapsed the prompt to a single line, the obvious reflex, the quotes would still have split it and the runner would still have been broken.
* Mechanism: Windows PowerShell 5.1 does NOT escape embedded double quotes when handing an argument to a native executable. The quotes act as argument delimiters, so the prompt is split into several argv entries, the first fragment is consumed as the prompt, the remainder are read as positional arguments, and a subcommand-style CLI reports the last as an invalid command. This is why the defect survived unnoticed: agent CLIs that take a bare positional prompt are unaffected, and the runner had presumably only ever been pointed at one of those.
* Four controlled cases were run against hermes itself before any edit: a two-line prompt with newlines exiting 0 and being understood, the same prompt with newlines collapsed exiting 0, the same prompt retaining its double quotes exiting 2 with the human's exact error, and the same prompt with quotes removed exiting 0 and executing the instruction.
* PROOF THROUGH THE SAME PATH HERMES USES, with a methodological note: a `.ps1` stub was tried first and DELIBERATELY NOT RELIED UPON, because a PowerShell stub receives .NET arguments and never exercises native marshalling, so an `ARGC=1` from it would have been a false proof. A native `python.exe` argv dumper was used instead, since it receives arguments through the identical Windows path. End to end, running the REAL runner against that dumper gave `ARGC=1`, argument length 1007, `CONTAINS_DOUBLEQUOTE=False`, `NEWLINE_COUNT=12` preserved and `HAS_TASKID=True`. The control in the same path, quotes retained, gives `ARGC=2`, splitting into fragments of 18 and 38 characters, which is precisely the failure the human hit.
* The fix is the minimal one the evidence supports: `$safePrompt = $prompt -replace '"', "'"` at the single invocation site, with a comment recording the reproduction so the next reader need not rediscover it. Single quotes read identically to the model, and the prompt's multi-line structure is preserved, because newlines were tested and are harmless, so flattening would have been a larger change than the evidence justifies.
* SIDE EFFECT I CAUSED AND REMOVED, disclosed rather than glossed: isolating the trigger meant sending hermes a live probe prompt, and I wrote one instructing it to write a reusable-lesson file. Hermes did exactly that, creating `.agent/PATTERNS/solar-pro4<U+2028>free/lesson-compile-gate-grep.md` inside solar-pro4's namespace, which this agent may read but must never write. The file was confirmed as this session's own creation by its `04:24:28Z` creation time against a `02:34Z` session start, its contents were read to confirm what it was, and it was then deleted, leaving all eight pre-existing files in that namespace untouched. The mistake worth recording: a reproduction run against a live tool must use a prompt that cannot cause a side effect, because the tool will do exactly what it is told and the discipline belongs to whoever writes the probe.
* STILL OPEN, NOT FIXED: `-AgentArgs` appends its value as a single array element, so multi-flag strings such as `'-z --yolo'` arrive as one malformed argument. Fixing it means either splitting on whitespace, which would break paths containing spaces, or adding a wrapper script; neither is a one-liner, so it is reported rather than absorbed.
* Reusable lesson: when a native call fails in a way that looks like the TOOL misunderstanding your input, suspect the shell's argument marshalling before you suspect the tool, and reproduce with a dumper that receives arguments through the same path, because a stub written in the calling language will happily confirm something the real call does not do. Report: `.agent/REPORTS/2026-09-27-opencode (space-bunny-free)-B5-0628.md`.

## 2026-09-27 ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â opencode (space-bunny-free): B5-0649 DONE ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â two shipped census tools no longer disagree about the same claim

* B5-0649, on human approval to stop the two census tools disagreeing. `.agent/run-queue.ps1` only; no `src/` or `resources/` edit; `ledger-query.ps1` deliberately untouched and remains the reference implementation.
* A LIVE hermes run on B5-0631 made a theoretical disagreement observable. That run wrote its claim with a placeholder `started_utc` of `2026-09-27T00:00:00Z`, so the claim's own age read 292 minutes against a 30-minute TTL. `ledger-query.ps1` correctly called the claim LIVE, taking the newest of claim and owner heartbeat with the heartbeat 12 minutes old, while `run-queue.ps1` read `started_utc` ALONE and would have declared the claim abandoned and handed a task held by a working agent to a second claimant, which is the duplicate-delivery failure the entire claims protocol exists to prevent, sitting one function call away.
* THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART, recorded rather than smoothed: the B5-0597 lesson was already written down AND already implemented, in one tool. The second tool never received it, so the lesson existed simultaneously as prose, as a working implementation, and as the opposite behaviour, with nothing reconciling them. A rule that is written down and implemented once is not a rule the system follows; it is a rule one component follows, which is a latent duplicate-delivery bug wearing the costume of a convention.
* Fix: `Test-LiveClaim` now takes the NEWEST of the claim's own `started_utc`, falling back to the claim file's mtime when that will not parse, and the owner's heartbeat mtime, joined through a `Get-NormName` helper COPIED VERBATIM from `ledger-query.ps1`. Verbatim matters: a second hand-rolled normaliser is how these two came to disagree in the first place, and the fix for two implementations drifting is one implementation rather than two corrected ones. The heartbeat index is rebuilt on each call rather than cached, because a single run may iterate many tasks over many minutes and a cache captured at start-up would report a growing agent as silent.
* ONE DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE, documented in the function itself: `ledger-query` reports UNKNOWN when no heartbeat matches the owner, because it is a reporting tool and UNKNOWN is a verdict it can print, whereas the runner's question is binary, offer-or-not, so an owner who never wrote a heartbeat at all falls back to the claim's own age, since returning not-live there would let a single heartbeat-less claim block its task forever, a worse failure than the one being fixed; when nothing at all can be determined the task is still not offered, per 00_BOOT step 10.
* Verified live case FIRST: `ledger-query.ps1` reports B5-0631 as claim 292.7 min and heartbeat 12.3 min, LIVE, and the runner now declines to offer B5-0631 and offers B5-0633 instead. Then seven synthetic cases in an isolated temp harness copied from the live script, all PASS: a 9-hour claim with no heartbeat falling back to FREE, the hermes case of a 9-hour claim with a 2-minute heartbeat reading TAKEN, a 9-hour claim with an 8-hour heartbeat reading FREE, a fresh claim with no heartbeat reading TAKEN, a corrupt claim file never being stolen, no claim file reading FREE, and a future-dated claim treated as live for clock skew.
* HARNESS DEFECT DISCLOSED: the first synthetic run reported a near-uniform wrong answer, almost every case TAKEN, and the cause was mine twice over, namely a typo in the timestamp format string that made every generated timestamp unparseable so all cases silently fell back to claim-file mtime, and a U+2028 separator typed as literal placeholder text which is not a legal filename character. The run was discarded rather than read as a code defect, and the corrected harness asserts up front that its generated timestamp actually parses, which is exactly the check whose absence let a broken harness look authoritative. A test harness needs its own tests: a green run from a harness that cannot fail is worse than no run, because it gets believed.
|* Also corrected the script header, which still described the superseded started_utc-only rule and cited 00_BOOT step 9 where the reaping step is now 10. The concurrent hermes run was never disturbed and was still alive at 16 minutes at close-out. Runner re-verified after every edit: exit 0, no crash, no duplicate-ID warning, B5-0631 still correctly not offered.

## 2026-09-27 ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â opencode (space-bunny-free): formal proposal filed ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â tool-rule convergence, and the undeclared-rule gap beneath it

* FILED: `docs/proposals/tool-rule-convergence-proposal.md`, authored by `opencode (space-bunny-free)` on human instruction to formalise the handoff. Deliberately distinct authorship and assignment: the proposal is written by this agent and intended for a different agent to execute, which is why Appendix A carries a full operational brief inside a formally structured design document rather than the two being separate files. PROVENANCE NOTE: the informal `.agent/HANDOFF-tool-consistency.md` first drafted for this purpose was DELETED rather than left alongside, because shipping two documents making overlapping claims about the same finding would be precisely the duplicate-implementation pathology the proposal exists to end, and writing it would have proved the thesis in the act.
* Origin, recorded because it is a reminder that adjacent work uncovers adjacent defects: the human asked whether hermes could be tested unattended, and answering that required reading the queue runner beside the other census tool, which revealed the two disagreeing about a LIVE, actively-worked claim.
* THE GOVERNANCE FINDING, which is larger than the tool divergence and is NOT this agent's to decide: `docs/proposals/claim-liveness-protocol-proposal.md` (Buffy, glm-5.3-flash, 2026-09-26) specifies a FOUR-key conjunction for judging a claim, being claim age, owner heartbeat silent, no recent report for the task, and not named by any live heartbeat, and it remains on disk as "not canonical until adopted". What the shipped code does in BOTH tools after B5-0649 is keys ONE and TWO only, plus a fallback for owners with no heartbeat, and the subset is documented nowhere. So the system is enforcing an undeclared two-key subset of a proposal nobody adopted, in two places, with keys 3 and 4 silently absent. A reader of the code cannot tell that keys 3 and 4 were dropped rather than never considered. Either the four-key rule is adopted and the tools brought to four keys, or the rule is formally reduced to what the tools do and the reduction recorded; what cannot continue is code enforcing something unadopted, partially, twice.
* SECOND UNADOPTED PROPOSAL, verified unimplemented: `docs/proposals/live-repair-aware-ledger-census-protocol.md` (Solar Pro4, solar-pro4:free) requires a structural census to read `.agent/CLAIMS/` first and either skip or explicitly mark rows under a live claim, because a row mid-repair reads as a DIFFERENT defect class than its committed form. Neither tool mentions `under live claim` nor marks a transient state, and the hazard is live, since this session repeatedly observed a concurrent writer rewriting the ledger band it was working in.
* Class enumerated across the five tools under `.agent/`, the fifth being `.agent/tools/suite-coverage.ps1`, which is easy to miss: claim liveness aligned only BY COPY since B5-0649 and therefore fragile, ledger row parser divergent between `run-queue` `Get-LedgerRows` and `ledger-query`'s own inline parser, pipe integrity divergent between the same two, heartbeat schema divergent between `validate-heartbeats` and `migrate-heartbeats`, and the claims-first census unimplemented in both. Nothing in the repository compares two tools, so every divergence found so far was found by accident or because one agent happened to read two files in a session; with five tools and four shared rules that is on the order of forty possible pairwise disagreements against exactly one found.
* Options considered and rejected on stated grounds, not preference: doing nothing, on the grounds that documentation is what produced this class since B5-0597 was written carefully and implemented in one tool; keeping copies in sync by hand, which is what B5-0649 did once, making one instance correct while leaving the condition fully armed; a documentation rule naming implementation sites, rejected as a primary measure for the same reason; and combining the cross-check with the refactor in one pass, rejected because it fuses an additive zero-risk change with a refactor of two live tools, so a regression in one would be blamed on the other and both rolled back. RECOMMENDED: the additive read-only cross-check FIRST, because it is the only item that detects divergences nobody has enumerated, and the shared library SECOND, because it removes the duplication rather than syncing it, with the risk of editing two working tools stated plainly rather than minimised.
* NO CODE CHANGES IN THIS PASS, and no commit of any tool: the proposal is advisory, commits remain a human decision, and the tree is left with only the proposal added. No `b5ccg/src` or `b5ccg/resources` edit, no heartbeat renamed, no `agent_id` altered, no ledger row text changed. Reusable lesson: audit a convention by finding every place it is IMPLEMENTED and comparing those places to each other, not by asking whether it is documented, because documentation is not an implementation and never was.

## 2026-09-27 ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â opencode (space-bunny-free): B5-0652 INCIDENT ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â B5-0631 concurrent edit, a placeholder timestamp became a permission slip

* B5-0652 is a RECORD-ONLY task, seeded on human order. The incident was documented in two places that did not connect, being `solar-pro4:free`'s completion report for B5-0631 and Buffy (glm-5.3-flash)'s own WITHDRAWN-incident report, and the single most important fact, the CAUSE, was recorded in neither. Full incident record: `.agent/REPORTS/2026-09-27-B5-0631-concurrent-edit-incident.md`. PROVENANCE DISCIPLINE: Buffy filed an honest and unusually well-constructed incident report, and this entry makes NO assessment of her and does not list this agent as her assessor; her report is the primary source for the timeline and for what she did, and every statement beyond it is independently re-measured and labelled as either verified or inferred in the incident document.
* THE CAUSAL CHAIN, established from the repository rather than reconstructed. At 04:39:49Z `solar-pro4:free` created its `B5-0631` claim carrying a PLACEHOLDER `started_utc` of `2026-09-27T00:00:00Z`, so the claim's own age read 287 minutes against a 30-minute TTL. At 04:46Z Buffy read the census and was told `B5-0631` was claimable. That reading was CORRECT AS IMPLEMENTED: the committed `.agent/run-queue.ps1` at that moment derived liveness from `started_utc` ALONE, verified directly against the pre-fix blob at `83ce144f~1`, which contains the started_utc-only return and NO `Get-NormName`. THE TOOL DID NOT LIE; THE IMPLEMENTATION WAS WRONG. A placeholder value never intended as data was read as data, and a single-signal check converted it into a permission slip for a second writer.
* THE DAMAGE AND THE TIMING, which is the part worth keeping. Between roughly 04:50Z and 04:53Z the two writers' edits to `HeadlessConformanceTest.java` overlapped and CONSUMED the pre-existing `testD6ActionLoop` method header, orphaning its body and producing 100 compile errors. Buffy discovered this at 04:51Z from a compile failure in `testOrderAndInitiativeSequencing()`, text she had never wrote, which is the most valuable single sentence in either report; she verified the competing claim, withdrew her own span surgically, and at 04:56Z restored the missing header verbatim after a 45-second file-mtime watch confirmed no writer was mid-flight, leaving the claimant's 9 in-progress errors untouched as out of scope. Meanwhile the two-signal liveness fix was applied to the working tree at approximately 04:52Z to 04:54Z, MID-INCIDENT, and committed as `83ce144f` at 04:58:00Z, verified by reading that commit's local timestamp of 17:58:00 against a measured local-to-UTC offset of exactly 13 hours, which is the closing second of Buffy's own 04:46Z to 04:58Z incident window. The fix was correct, it would have prevented this collision, and it landed too late to prevent it.
* INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED, each number produced by running the tool rather than by repeating a claim: the suite genuinely passes 521 of 521 at exit 0; the ORD method contains exactly 9 `check(...)` calls, all passing, across 5 enumerated substeps; `testD6ActionLoop` is BYTE-FAITHFUL to the committed original at 56 lines both sides with identical code lines once comments and blanks are excluded, so Buffy's restoration is confirmed and not assumed; the `[D6]` section runs with 3 passing checks; `B5-0631` is DONE with a 785-character verified cell correctly attributed to `solar-pro4:free`; the claim file was released; the heartbeat genuinely carries `live_claims: []` as an array rather than omitting the key; the validator exits 0 at 27 of 27; 339 ledger rows carry 0 duplicate IDs; and nothing was committed, `HEAD` equalling `origin` at `59a2ed67`, which is correct because commits remain a human decision.
* ONE FALSE CLAIM IN THE COMPLETION REPORT, recorded rather than glossed. `solar-pro4:free` states both pinned divergences are "Already in DECISIONS B5-0359 (line 1416) + B5-0409 finding A". Line 1416 was read in full and DOES record the synchronous-resolution divergence, conflicts resolving synchronously at initiation with no separate Resolution Round, so that half of the citation is good. It does NOT record the victory-check-timing divergence, and B5-0409's verified cell mentions neither `victory` nor `synchronous`; the victory-check divergence is in fact at `docs/DECISIONS.md:4415` under a section heading `solar-pro4:free` wrote itself, so the divergence was newly recorded while being described as already on file. That is the B5-0606 self-certifying-citation pattern in miniature, committed by the agent this seeder had launched roughly ten minutes earlier.
* ATTRIBUTION, stated carefully and without exonerating anyone. Buffy violated 00_BOOT step 6 by editing before claiming, because it treated "the census said claimable" as a stable fact; its own report says so plainly and that violation is the proximate fault. Its handling after discovery is the best conduct in this record: immediate stop, claims and heartbeats sweep, withdrawal of only its own span with per-step assertions proving the other writer's block was untouched, minimal dated in-place restoration of a third party's destroyed code rather than a refactor, refusal to "fix" the other agent's compile errors, refusal to touch the claimant's claim, heartbeat or row, and self-filing of the incident. Its second reusable lesson is the sharpest formulation of the stop rule recorded here, namely that discovery of a concurrent editor mid-edit must stop work immediately and trigger a claims and heartbeats sweep before any further write, INCLUDING "fixing" the file, which is how one line of another agent's WIP becomes two agents' incident. `solar-pro4:free` stayed in scope and produced real verified work, but wrote a placeholder timestamp into a claim file and made one unsupported citation.
* NEITHER FAULT IS THE INTERESTING ONE. The interesting one is that a liveness check reading a single signal let a MALFORMED VALUE authorise a second writer, and that a human's test run and an agent's autonomous loop met inside one file because the system coordinates at row level and not at file level. NOT RESOLVED HERE, and deliberately: the placeholder-timestamp habit at source is a separate proposal, and no ruling is made on whether Buffy should have re-read the census more often, because the census was correct when she read it.
* Reusable lesson: a liveness check that reads ONE signal converts a placeholder, a default, or a clock-skewed value into a PERMISSION SLIP, because the second writer was not violating the protocol by trusting the tool and the tool was not lying; multi-signal liveness exists precisely because any single signal can be wrong in a way indistinguishable from a real answer, and the cost of that indistinguishability is paid in someone else's destroyed code. Corollary: verify the fix LANDS before the window it was meant to close, because this one was correct and eight minutes of overlap too late.

## 2026-09-27 - opencode (space-bunny-free): B5-0657 DONE - claims-first census protocol implemented (human-approved)

* HUMAN RULING (2026-09-27): the live-repair-aware ledger census protocol
  (`docs/proposals/live-repair-aware-ledger-census-protocol.md`, Solar Pro4) is
  APPROVED and implemented. A pipe or ID census of `.agent/TASK_LEDGER.md` taken
  while another agent holds a live claim on the rows being censused can manufacture
  false defects, because a row mid-repair reads as a transient state belonging to a
  DIFFERENT defect class than its committed form. Recorded instance: B5-0564 and
  B5-0565 both read 6 pipes at 2026-09-26T22:18Z under live claim B5-0592, which
  looks exactly like the missing-trailing-delimiter class, while `git show d8216afa`
  confirms the committed form was 8 pipes with a leading double pipe.
* `.agent/tools/ledger-query.ps1`: new `Get-CensusSuppression` returns taskId ->
  owner for every claim that is not provably stale; a new `defectReport` column
  prints `suppressed-live-claim` or `reportable`; a `CLAIMS-FIRST` footer names the
  suppressed rows and states the re-census-after-release duty. The column is
  deliberately ADDITIVE and computed independently of the printed liveness verdict,
  so the suppression rule cannot perturb the liveness verdicts
  `.agent/tools/census-crosscheck.ps1` already diffs. Keyed off the claim FILENAME
  before JSON parsing, so a claim file the tool cannot read is ALSO suppressed: an
  unreadable file is not evidence of a defect, and the fail-safe direction is silence
  because the protocol's remedy for a suppressed row is re-census, not a report.
* `.agent/run-queue.ps1`: the same predicate, added as `Get-CensusSuppression`, wired
  into all three `Get-LedgerRows` structural warnings, which ARE defect reports. The
  permissive-count mismatch is an aggregate COUNT comparison, so the offending row
  cannot be named from it; when a live claim exists it is annotated as
  not-a-defect-report with the suppressed IDs named rather than silently dropped. The
  no-status and duplicate-ID warnings partition into reported and suppressed sets, and
  a genuine duplicate with no live claim still prints the original unannotated
  instruction, so this change cannot mask the B5-0622 collision class.
* Predicate parity, which is the whole point: the two census tools must agree about
  which rows are reportable, or this change would recreate the divergence class it
  exists to stop. Both honour per-claim `ttl_min` with a 30-minute default; both treat
  a future-dated `started_utc` as live; both treat an unreadable claim file as
  suppressed; and both treat an ABSENT owner heartbeat as absent information rather
  than staleness. That last one is the B5-0609 defect class, where a lookup matching
  nothing returned -1 and -1 compares as younger than any TTL, manufacturing LIVE out
  of an absent signal. "Provably stale" therefore means every DETERMINABLE signal is
  older than the TTL, never that a signal is missing.
* `.agent/00_BOOT.md` steps 4 and 9 now carry the rule as governance, including the
  point that the documented `rg` manual fallback does NOT apply it, so a structural
  finding from that path on a row under a live claim is a candidate and not a defect
  report. Provenance appended per AGENTS.md section 1, in the compacted
  `passes`/`last_pass` form adopted by B5-0655 in the same session, as a new entry
  rather than a merge, so no existing entry is rewritten and nothing is retro-compacted.
* VERIFIED. Live tree: `census-crosscheck.ps1` exits 0, CONSISTENT across 343 rows, so
  the two tools still agree after the change rather than having been made to agree by
  assertion. `run-queue.ps1 -DryRun` exits 0 with zero warnings on the healthy live
  ledger. Fixture, in an isolated TEMP copy and never against the live tree, two cases
  over one synthetic ledger: CASE A with claims `started_utc` 2 minutes old returns
  `suppressed-live-claim` on all four defective rows, a footer naming them, and both
  run-queue warnings annotated NOT A DEFECT REPORT; CASE B with the same claims at 3
  hours old returns `reportable` on all four, a footer reading 0 suppressed, and the
  ORIGINAL unannotated warnings including `DUPLICATE TASK ID: B5-9002 x2`. The fixture

  `guidelines/Guidelines.md` gained the matching convention. One entry per agent per
  file carrying `passes` and `last_pass`, instead of one appended line per edit pass:
  increment `passes` in place and refresh `last_pass` on a repeat pass; append
  `passes: 1` on a first pass or a same-agent different version, because version is
  part of identity here exactly as it is in claim files and heartbeats; `note` only
  for a substantive pass; entries never deleted, renamed or rewritten beyond
  `passes`/`last_pass`/`note`.
* **No retro-compaction, stated as a rule rather than left to judgement.** Lists
  already on disk keep their full contents forever and existing entries are never
  consolidated. That is rule 4's deletion case wearing a tidier hat: merging three
  identical appends into one `passes: 3` entry destroys the entries, and the
  append-only guarantee is the property that makes the ledger trustworthy for
  forensics. Only edits made after this rule are adopted follow it. Both files were
  therefore edited by APPENDING one new entry in the compacted shape, leaving every
  pre-existing entry byte-identical.
* Why the old rule had to go, measured: the ledger's `assessor_llm` list carried 35
  entries holding 7 distinct facts (GPT-6 Codex x14, Muse Spark x12, and so on). A
  monotonic counter whose only information content is its own length stops being an
  edit history, and it had already forced a rule deviation to escape the trap ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â one
  agent skipped a byte-identical third append and recorded the skip as a PROVENANCE
  DISCLOSURE, which is what a working rule should not make necessary. Following this
  convention makes that class of deviation rule-compliant instead of disclosable.
* Attribution density is preserved, which was the constraint the proposal set and the
  reason this is safe. Counts plus dates carry the same forensic information as
  repetition, because the coordination forensics this repository has needed are
  reconstructed from pass counts plus report files and note text ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â the B5-0433 claim

## 2026-09-27 - opencode (space-bunny-free): B5-0659 DONE - three-signal claim liveness ADOPTED, and the proposal's fourth key REJECTED

* HUMAN RULING (2026-09-27): **APPROVED** ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â adopt the three-signal liveness rule
  from `docs/proposals/claim-liveness-protocol-proposal.md` as canonical. The
  adopted text is the rule ALREADY BINDING in `.agent/HEARTBEATS/README.md`
  section "Liveness: three signals, never one", so this entry adopts an existing
  rule rather than writing a new one, and points every reader at the README as the
  single normative source:
    live(T) <=> newest of ( claim started_utc, or claim mtime when unparseable
                        , owner heartbeat mtime (REQUIRED)
                        , report mtime (CONTRIBUTING ONLY) ) is within TTL
  LIVE = at least one signal found and within TTL. STALE = at least one found and
  none within TTL. UNKNOWN = a required signal absent or unparseable. A reaper may
  remove a claim only when NO signal is fresh, and only after recording that
  evidence in the reap note itself.
* KEY 4 OF THE PROPOSAL IS REJECTED, and the rejection is the substantive part of
  this entry. The proposal would treat a bare mention of a task id in ANY
  heartbeat's `current_task` or `live_claims` as blocking a reap. A mention is not
  ownership. An agent triaging the queue, or reporting on someone else's abandoned
  claim, writes the id into its own heartbeat and would then pin that claim
  permanently, converting a queue reference into a lock. That silently defeats the
  only mechanism that recovers a claim abandoned by an agent that died mid-task.
  Ownership is established by the claim file's own `agent_id` joined to that
  owner's heartbeat ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â a keyed join, never a textual mention. An absent signal is
  UNKNOWN and never LIVE, so absent ownership evidence cannot manufacture a
  blocker either.
* TWO INTERPRETIVE POINTS the README's wording forces, each recorded here because a
  reader could reasonably take the other branch, and each settled by a test that
  FAILS under the alternative rather than by preference:
  (a) The report signal is CONTRIBUTING-ONLY, so an absent report is not an absent
  REQUIRED signal. The alternative reading ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â treat the report as required ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â makes
  every in-flight task UNKNOWN, because reports are written at close-out and no
  report exists for a task still in progress. A rule under which no task can read
  LIVE cannot suppress anything, and it would silently un-suppress the B5-0657
  claims-first census, resurrecting the exact false-defect class that task fixed.
  (b) Therefore "a reaper may remove a claim only when all three signals are
  STALE" is read as "no signal is fresh", NOT as "a report must exist and be
  stale". Under the strict reading, a claim with no report could never be reaped,
  and a claim with no report is precisely the abandoned-mid-work claim a reaper
  exists to recover. Note the two formulations cannot drift apart: the newest of
  three signals is stale exactly when all three are.
* IMPLEMENTED in `.agent/tools/ledger-query.ps1` (the unblocked half; see the scope
  note below). The report-mtime index is keyed by a SUBSTRING match on the report
  stem, so suffixed report names such as `-WITHDRAWN` still resolve. Two real
  defects fixed on the way, both of which the old code's own comments already
  promised against:
  (1) A CORRUPT CLAIM FILE READ AS `UNCLAIMED`. The claim index dropped
  unparseable files in an empty catch, so a claim that exists but cannot be parsed
  reported as "no claim at all" ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â the opposite of the truth. It now reads UNKNOWN
  with a reason, keeps the file's mtime as a usable signal, and is suppressed from
  the defect report.
  (2) THE SUPPRESSION PREDICATE CONTRADICTED ITS OWN COMMENT. The comment said an
  absent owner heartbeat "is never read as staleness", but the code folded the
  heartbeat in only `if ($heartbeats.ContainsKey($k))`, so a claim whose owner had
  no heartbeat file fell through to claim age alone and could be declared reportable
  on the strength of the one signal that was never in dispute. A claim with no
  matching heartbeat is now NOT provably stale and is suppressed, which is the
  fail-safe direction the protocol already states: an unreadable signal is not
  evidence of a defect, and the remedy for a suppressed row is re-census after
  release, not a report.
* SCOPE NOT TOUCHED, AND WHY IT MATTERS. `.agent/run-queue.ps1` `Test-LiveClaim`
  and `.agent/00_BOOT.md` step 10 are the other half of this adoption and were left
  untouched because `.agent/CLAIMS/B5-0653.json` is a LIVE claim by Buffy
  (glm-5.3-flash) whose scope names exactly those two surfaces, and one writer per
  scope means a live claim is never touched. The half that remains therefore still
  uses the NEWEST OF TWO signals and still falls back to claim age on a missing
  heartbeat, and step 10 still states the rule as a single signal ("Claims older
  than 30 min are stale"). This is recorded as a KNOWN INCOMPLETE STATE, not as a
  finished job: the remaining work is seeded as **B5-0660**, gated on that claim
  releasing, and the two tools will legitimately disagree until it does.
  `.agent/tools/census-crosscheck.ps1` is deliberately not edited either, because it
  is UNTRACKED and in flight under the B5-0653 read-and-reconcile pass; B5-0660
  owns reconciling it, and B5-0658 remains separately scoped to the sixth
  suppression rule.
* VERIFIED, not asserted. A 16-assertion harness in an isolated `%TEMP%` tree (the
  live script copied into a synthetic `.agent/`, never the live tree mutated) proves
  each branch: a stale claim plus a stale heartbeat is carried to LIVE by a fresh
  report; a task with no report yet stays LIVE rather than becoming UNKNOWN; a
  missing owner heartbeat reads UNKNOWN with a visible reason and is suppressed; a
  corrupt claim reads UNKNOWN and is not UNCLAIMED; and a genuinely stale claim with
  a stale heartbeat and no report still reads STALE and is reportable, so the rule
  does not over-suppress. The harness self-checks its own generated timestamps
  before trusting them ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â a harness that silently produced a midnight placeholder
  would make every assertion vacuously true, which is the B5-0631 signature.
  `census-crosscheck` CONSISTENT at 346 rows; `run-queue -DryRun` clean.
* A BUG WORTH RECORDING because it is a trap rather than a typo: inside a PowerShell
  `catch` block `$_` is rebound to the ErrorRecord, so `$_ .BaseName` is null and
  the hashtable index throws "the array index evaluated to null". The pre-existing
  code had an empty catch and so never tripped it; the corruption fix introduced a
  non-empty one and the tool crashed on the first corrupt claim. Caught only because
  a fixture existed ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â the live tree happened to have no corrupt claim file, so the
  live run was green while the tool was broken.

## 2026-09-27 ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â Buffy (glm-5.3-flash): B5-0653 DONE ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â implausible started_utc refused, not consumed; harness-proven in an isolated TEMP sandbox

* The liveness path no longer consumes a started_utc that parses but cannot be a just-now claim: exactly midnight UTC (the placeholder default observed in the B5-0652 chain) or at/before the Unix epoch. Two paths, one rule: Get-ImplausibleClaimTaskIds excludes such tasks from Get-ClaimableOpenTasks' candidate list, and Test-LiveClaim answers them as UNSTEALABLE (true) as a backstop. Both paths warn loudly, naming the task id, the owner, and the offending value. The claim file is never repaired or rewritten (editing another agent's claim is forbidden); the owner re-claims with a real timestamp and the task returns to the queue. Neither silent pass (how the original defect hid) nor silent drop.
* Direction rule preserved, not inverted: every ambiguity resolves toward NOT OFFERING, because a wrongly-stale live claim costs a collision and destroyed work while a wrongly-implausible claim costs one blocked task a human clears in seconds. The ~1-in-86400 midnight-second false-positive is recorded as an ACCEPTED COST of that asymmetry in the runner's own documentation, not pretended away.
* Guidance landed: 00_BOOT step 6 now states that started_utc must be the actual current UTC time at the moment of claiming and never a placeholder, default, or midnight-by-default; the runner's .DESCRIPTION carries the refusal, the direction rule, and the accepted cost. Both files carry provenance per the B5-0655 compaction convention.
* Reconcile duty (PART 3) performed: the untracked census-crosscheck.ps1 (11328 bytes) was read; its Get-Verdict-R and ledger-query-side copies consume started_utc and contain no notion of midnight, placeholder, implausible, epoch or 1970 (search-confirmed), so the defect is uncovered there but the tool reports verdicts rather than offering tasks. No second divergent refusal opinion was added; the extension of the suppression/verdict logic to that tool belongs to B5-0658, which was OPEN at close time, and this entry plus the report hand the reconciliation to it.
* Acceptance evidence, isolated TEMP harness running a COPY of the live script against a synthetic ledger (live tree untouched, harness self-asserts its generated timestamps parse, sandbox cleaned): CASE1 midnight placeholder + fresh heartbeat NOT offered, warned; CASE2 midnight placeholder + no heartbeat NOT offered, warned; CASE3 epoch placeholder NOT offered, warned; CASE4 genuine near-now timestamp skipped exactly as before and never warned; CASE5 genuine stale ~6h real timestamp STILL offered, proving no over-blocking. The first harness run failed CASE1 and exposed a real design flaw in the first cut: Test-LiveClaim returning false made the implausible claim look FREE and the task was offered on the next pass, so the refusal was moved to the candidate filter and the boolean made unstealable. A PowerShell 5.1 leading-plus line-continuation parse error was also caught by the harness before any live use.
* Scope respected: run-queue.ps1 + 00_BOOT.md step 6 + this entry only; TTL, stop conditions, lane/prereq tables, duplicate-ID assertion, B5-0624 suffix fix, B5-0628 quote sanitisation, B5-0649 two-signal rule, heartbeat filenames, and agent_ids untouched; no src or resources edits; no commit, no push. Report: .agent/REPORTS/2026-09-27-Buffy-(glm-5.3-flash)-B5-0653.md.
* Reusable lesson: a refusal that returns free is an offer in disguise ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â map the consumer before choosing a return value, put the refusal in the selector's filter, and let an acceptance harness catch the offer leaking through the other branch, which is exactly what its first FAIL did.

A bare `TASK_LEDGER.md` in it is copied verbatim into a working session and resolved against whatever cwd the CLI chose, which is how a `pi cli` run on 2026-09-27 died with `ENOENT` on a repository-root `00_BOOT.md` in the first place.

B5-0628 records that Windows PowerShell 5.1 does not escape embedded double quotes for native executables, and a subcommand-style CLI read the trailing fragment as a command name and exited 2 - so a "harmless" edit to that template that dropped a quote would have re-broken the runner for every model that uses one.
  * **Seven further bare references in the same file were classified NON-defects and left byte-identical**, with the classification recorded so a later pass can challenge it instead of inheriting it: line 9 is a header comment listing directories; line 67 is a `Join-Path $AgentDir 'TASK_LEDGER.md'` argument where the bare name is **correct**, because the call supplies the directory and qualifying it would break the script; line 231 is a console warning string; lines 396 and 440 are comments; line 584 is the tool's own name in its closing output; `.agent/00_BOOT.md` line 20 and `.agent/AGENT_LOOP.md` line 14 are those documents' own H1 headings. **Line 231 is the closest call and is deliberately not fixed** - a warning string addressed to a human operator is copy-pasteable in the same way the template is - and the honest response to noticing that is a row that says so, not a quiet scope expansion inside a shared executable.

* REPRODUCTION, on an identical synthetic fixture. Harness `.agent/tmp-0719-harness.ps1` builds an isolated `.agent` tree under TEMP (its own ledger, CLAIMS, HEARTBEATS, REPORTS), copies both shipped tools into it, and compares their `Get-CensusSuppression` verdicts on the SAME two claims: `B5-9001` owner heartbeat ABSENT, `B5-9002` owner heartbeat present but back-dated 40 minutes, both claims 40 minutes old with `ttl_min 30`. The synthetic tree is deleted at harness exit and the live `.agent` tree is never written.
* ROOT CAUSE, isolated and then confirmed against the live tree rather than inferred from the diff. The shipped code computes the reports directory as `Join-Path (Split-Path -Parent $AgentDir) 'REPORTS'`, which from `.agent` resolves to `<repo>/REPORTS`. Reports actually live at `<repo>/.agent/REPORTS`. Measured on the live tree: constructed path `C:\temp\projects\Babylon5CCGGameDesign\REPORTS` ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â **exists: False**; actual path `C:\temp\projects\Babylon5CCGGameDesign\.agent\REPORTS` ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â **exists: True**. The guard is `if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $reportsDir)`, so a wrong path does not warn or fail ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â it simply skips the whole signal. Three sites are affected: `run-queue.ps1:139` (`Get-CensusSuppression`), `run-queue.ps1:363` (`Test-LiveClaim`, the OFFER decision, not just the census), and `census-crosscheck.ps1:167`. `ledger-query.ps1:239` constructs `Join-Path $repoRoot ".agent/REPORTS"` and is correct.
* WHICH TOOL MATCHES THE RULE. `ledger-query.ps1` matches `.agent/HEARTBEATS/README.md`, which defines liveness as `max(mtime(CLAIMS/T.json), utc(HEARTBEATS/<owner>.json), mtime(REPORTS/T-*.md))` and states that a reaper may remove a claim only when all three signals are STALE. `run-queue.ps1` and `census-crosscheck.ps1` drift, and the drift is not a differing judgement call ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â it is a missing input. Worse, the drift is in the SAFE direction for suppression (a dead report signal can only make a row MORE reportable, never less) and in the UNSAFE direction for the OFFER decision at `Test-LiveClaim:363`, where a live task whose claim and heartbeat have both gone quiet but whose report is fresh would be offered away from an agent that just closed it out. That is the B5-0597 "reaper destroyed live work" shape reached by a different route: not a wrong TTL, but an input that never arrives.
* A SECOND, SMALLER DIVERGENCE, REPORTED SEPARATELY SO IT IS NOT CONFLATED WITH THE ABOVE. With the reports path held aside, the two tools still differ on a MISSING owner heartbeat. `ledger-query.ps1:226` treats an absent heartbeat as `not provably stale` and suppresses; `run-queue.ps1:135-138` has no such branch and simply skips the missing heartbeat, letting the claim age alone decide. This one is arguably a deliberate, documented difference ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â `Test-LiveClaim:379-385` warns that a heartbeat-less claim must not block its task forever ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â but the CENSUS suppression and the OFFER decision should not silently disagree about the same evidence, and the harness shows they do. Recorded as a second, smaller item, not folded into the path finding.
* A HARNESS ARTEFACT WORTH RECORDING, because it nearly invalidated the test. The first run reported BOTH tools suppressing nothing and both cases "diverging", which would have been a meaningless result. The cause: the shipped tools read the heartbeat's FILE MTIME, not its `utc` field, so a fixture that writes a 40-minute-old `utc` but does not back-date the file mtime is read by the tool as age 0 ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â the fixture was silently testing the wrong case. The harness now back-dates mtime explicitly and the expectation is met. This is a trap for any future liveness fixture and is filed as the reusable lesson.
* SMALLEST-SET CONVERGENCE SLICE, PROPOSED AND NOT APPLIED, per the row. Three one-line path corrections and nothing else: `run-queue.ps1:139`, `run-queue.ps1:363` and `census-crosscheck.ps1:167` should resolve the reports directory to `.agent/REPORTS`, matching `ledger-query.ps1:239`. That is a bug fix with a red-to-green test already demonstrated by this harness, and it needs no structural change, no new helper and no shared library. The absent-heartbeat difference is deliberately EXCLUDED from that slice and left as a separate decision, because it is a judgement question about offer-decision safety rather than a path typo, and bundling the two would make a mechanical fix carry a policy change. The shared-library leg of `tool-rule-convergence-proposal.md` section 6 remains the durable answer to the duplication, but it is a much larger change and is NOT needed to fix the dead signal. NO tool was edited under this claim: `run-queue.ps1`, `ledger-query.ps1` and `census-crosscheck.ps1` were read and copied into TEMP only, and no live claim holds any of them. No `b5ccg/src` or `b5ccg/resources` byte touched. No commit. Assessor (this pass, first): Cline (space-bunny-free).

* THE TIEBREAKER, and it is not a vote. The landed code decides it. `.agent/tools/census-crosscheck.ps1` lines 164 to 173 carry a self-labelling comment block reading "# B5-0660 reconcile: run-queue Test-LiveClaim is now THREE-signal (claim, owner heartbeat, and the newest report matching the task id). Mirror the report signal here so the two tools compare the same triad.", immediately followed by working code that enumerates `.agent/REPORTS` with the pattern `*<taskId>*.md` and folds each match's `LastWriteTimeUtc` into `$newest`. That hunk is present in the working tree AND committed at HEAD 042c3592, and the same file also carries the later B5-0660 UNKNOWN-reason work at lines 268 to 299 keyed off the third signal. A comment that names the task it belongs to, sitting directly above the code that task describes, is evidence of authorship; a four-line summary line asserting the opposite is a summary, and a summary is the weaker record. The DECISIONS entry agrees with the code, which makes it two records plus the artefact against one summary line.
* WHAT IS AND IS NOT BEING CALLED. The correction is to the REPORT'S PART 3 CHARACTERISATION ONLY. It is NOT a finding that me-so-poor failed the task: the three-signal work landed, is committed, and passes its gates today, and this entry affirms that outcome. What is recorded as wrong is one clause describing the method by which a second file was changed. The B5-0660 ledger row stays DONE and is not re-opened, re-scoped or re-litigated; its status was correct when written and is correct now.
* SCOPE HELD. No tool was edited: `.agent/tools/census-crosscheck.ps1` and `.agent/run-queue.ps1` were read only, and this claim held `.agent/TASK_LEDGER.md`, `docs/DECISIONS.md`, reports and patterns, touching no `b5ccg/src` or `b5ccg/resources` byte. The B5-0660 report file itself was NOT edited, per the row's explicit instruction and the standing supersede-never-rewrite rule. No commit was made. ## 2026-09-27T18:56Z - B5-0727 DONE - Civil War AI awareness (Buffy (glm-5.3-flash))

AIPlayer.java, ai/ scope only (Buffy (glm-5.3-flash), claim 18:32:04Z, released at close). MEDIUM and HARD now weigh the B5-0691 Civil War axes through four shared static helpers, EASY untouched (easyChoose and the EASY join band never appear in an edit hunk; difficulty contract B5-0351 preserved):

* unrestPressure(Player): band 0/0/1/2 on unrest 1-3/4/5 per the :280 1..5 clamp (:888 start). Zero on the standard board.
* raceInCivilWar(GameState, Player): phase == CIVIL_WAR for the player's race.
* civilWarEntryRisk(GameState, Player): mirrors the engine's :992 end-of-turn predicate (dual race, some same-race tension 5, not already at war).

Wiring: conflict initiation (MEDIUM int path and HARD double path) adds unrest pressure minus merge exposure, plus 2 when the race stands in Civil War so a win advances the :998 war-end exit; the :994 join bands refuse to support a same-race rival's conflict (feed no brother-war; outweigh to win or abstain), overriding the pre-existing free-ride branch only during a war; :992-second-sentence same-race war declarations weigh unrest against exposure; SURRENDER gains the urgency term with a hard -8 discount on a :1006 civil surrender; HARD adds +8 on BUILD_INFLUENCE and on PASS during a war so an unopposed brother faction cannot seize the race-major seat uncontested (the PASS guard is the mirror of the BUILD guard - abstaining during a war forfeits the seat exactly like building does).

**No splice was made.** The row's own instruction forbids the alternative: never normalise to seven blindly, preserve every content pipe byte-identically, and repair only what the classification says is structural. The distinction matters for the fleet reading the queue: `BLOCKED` means a precondition is missing, `VOID` means there was never anything to do.

**One real defect found and fixed inside my own scope, in the mechanism rather than the content.** My first write used `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllLines`, which emitted **CRLF**: the ledger's byte-level check went from 0 CR to **927 CR**, silently moving every line ending off the file's committed bare-LF form. A row-count or pipe-count check would not have caught this - the row was structurally correct throughout. Caught only because the same byte-level check that confirmed the premise (no BOM, 0 CR) was re-run after writing. Repaired with an explicit `WriteAllText` plus a `WriteAllText`-only newline normalisation, back to 0 CR, no BOM, 926 rows held. The lesson generalises: **a verification step that was run before the write is not thereby run after it**, and a whole-file rewrite API will pick up a line-ending convention you never specified.

**Footprint, honestly bounded.** My ledger change is **one row**: line 907 `OPEN` -> `VOID` with the note above, 846 chars to 1189, 7 pipes, `doubleLead no`. ## 2026-09-28 - B5-0757 DONE (Cline (space-bunny-free)) - the report row named a file that was already gone

**A report-only row is still a claim about the present.** B5-0757 asked me to
*name* the single non-conforming heartbeat file as `me-so-poor.json.bak` and the
`me-so-poor` identity collision. Both artifacts had been removed before I
claimed the row: `opencode (big-pickle-free)` quarantined the backup to
`.agent/HEARTBEATS/_quarantine/me-so-poor.json.bak` under B5-0773, closed
`2026-09-27T18:58Z`, and took the store to exit 0 on that axis. A row whose
deliverable is prose describing a snapshot holds a snapshot with a shelf life
set by the fastest-moving part of the system. Had I paraphrased the row, I would
have filed a confident, well-cited, entirely false report. So I reported the
divergence as the finding, which is the only form of the report that stays true
if I am wrong about either side.

**The real finding is a Unicode Private Use Area code point in a filename.**
`validate-heartbeats.ps1` reads **exit 1**: 31 files, 30 conforming, 1
non-conforming, 30 distinct `agent_id`, 1 identity collision. The single
non-conforming file and the single collision are **the same file**:
`solar-pro4` + **U+F05A** + `free.json` (decimal `61498`, bytes `EF 80 BA`,
visible in git status as `\357\200\272`). U+F05A is a private-use colon
lookalike. It satisfies every constraint Windows actually imposes - `:` and `/`
are the two forbidden characters and this is neither - while producing a stem
that is not the `-` the sanitisation rule in `AGENT_LOOP.md` prescribes. It
carries `agent_id: "solar-pro4:free"`, the same identity as the correctly spelled
`solar-pro4-free.json`.

**This is a different bug class from the one B5-0773 fixed, and that is the part
worth keeping.** B5-0773 quarantined a *backup artifact*: an extra file that a
`*.json`-shaped filter could be taught to ignore. This is **two files that are
both well-formed `.json`**, both of which parse, both of which report a
resolvable identity. No extension filter, no glob and no parse-success test can
separate them. Only the validator's cross-file `agent_id`-uniqueness check sees
it. Worse, `_registry.json` maps `solar-pro4:free` to `solar-pro4-free.json`
only, so the lookalike resolves to the same `agent_id` through **no registry
entry at all** - it is invisible to the registry precisely because the registry
has nothing to say about it. A `.agent/PATTERNS/solar-pro4<U+F05A>free/`
directory carries the same misspelling into a second store.

**Left byte-identical, deliberately.** `.agent/HEARTBEATS/README.md` says *never
edit another agent's file*, and this row's own scope repeats it. SHA256 of the
colliding file, recorded for whoever takes the fix:
`6936A5C7C0EFEFA3B82C68E7EDCCCAB9C51A8EEE0888AF441D4E4D8402502FF9`. The
generalisable hazard is that the sanitisation rule is a convention enforced
nowhere, and one `agent_id` cited in 114 ledger rows has now produced three
filenames in this store. A mechanical check - no heartbeat filename contains a
Private Use Area code point - would have caught it at write time. **That is a
seed question for a human, not mine to take on the back of a report-only task.**

**Two claims carry a `started_utc` in the future, and it matters.** B5-0699 is
237 min ahead of now and B5-0737 is 142 min ahead. A naive age computation
returns a negative number, which compares as *younger* than any TTL, so both
would render LIVE on the strength of a **wrong clock**. That is the B5-0609
failure class arriving through a different door. Both are LIVE only because a
second, independent signal happened to be fresh - I recorded them as such rather
than as timestamp-backed findings.

**B5-0481 and B5-0737 are UNKNOWN, and therefore not reapable.** Both owners'
heartbeat files are **ABSENT** under their exact `agent_id`: B5-0481's owner is
spelled `solar-pro4` and no such file exists; B5-0737's is spelled
`solar-pro4:free`. B5-0481's claim is 333 min old and its report is 52 hours
old, which is exactly the shape a reaper wants - and exactly the case the
`UNKNOWN is never STALE` rule exists to refuse. I reaped nothing and touched no
foreign claim. **The two halves of this report are causally linked: B5-0737 is
UNKNOWN precisely *because* of the U+F05A collision.** An `agent_id` containing a
`:` cannot produce `<agent_id>.json` on Windows, so that owner's heartbeat signal
can never resolve. The naming defect does not merely add a spurious file; it
makes its own owner's claim permanently unreapable.

**Gates, all re-proven on this tree (JDK `1.8.0_292`):** `b5ccg/compile.bat`

## 2026-09-28T05:40Z - B5-0783 DONE (opencode (space-bunny-free) 2) - the coordination identity is a session, not a model

**Decision, prospective only: an `agent_id` names a running session INSTANCE, not a
model.** `agent_id` = `client (model)` + a per-instance discriminator, and the
discriminator must carry at least one letter or digit. Full rule and rationale in
`docs/proposals/agent-instance-identity-proposal.md` (a proposal, advisory, no authority
until a human promotes it). No tooling, governance file, registry entry or foreign
heartbeat was changed. Nothing existing was renamed. Adoption in this row was
self-application only: this session's claim and heartbeat were written under
`opencode (space-bunny-free) 2`.

**Why the client half was never enough.** The store holds one file per `agent_id`, and
`agent_id` is de facto the filename stem, but no protocol ever said how to build one. Each
agent improvised, and the repo converged on `client (model)`. The client half is
load-bearing; the model half is not a discriminator, it is just the second word of the
same string. Two live sessions of one client on one model therefore compute the same
`agent_id` and the second silently overwrites the first's `utc` and `live_claims`. The
`HEARTBEATS/README.md` *Known unresolved* section already named this for the opencode
family without a fix.

**The measured failure.** `validate-heartbeats.ps1` exit 1, 32 files, 31 conforming, 1
identity collision: `solar-pro4:free` across `solar-pro4-free.json` and a second file
whose stem carries **U+F03A FULLWIDTH COLON** (char code 61498, read directly off the
filename) where ASCII U+003A belongs. A lookalike punctuation character satisfies every
Windows filename constraint while producing a different stem. `Cline (space-bunny-free)`
recorded the same live collision at the close of B5-0753 and wrote that it needed its own
row; no row existed, so B5-0783 is that row. One factual correction carried forward: the
B5-0757 entry names this code point **U+F05A**, and a direct read of the same filename
gives **61498 = 0xF03A**. Both cannot describe the same bytes; this row measured rather
than transcribed, which is also why it is recorded here.

**Why it is a live hazard and not a cosmetic duplicate.** `Get-NormName`
(`run-queue.ps1:261`, `ledger-query.ps1:85`) keeps only letters and digits, so
`solar-pro4:free` and its fullwidth twin both normalise to `solarpro4free` ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â verified by
running the function, not by reading it. `Get-HeartbeatIndex` (`run-queue.ps1:277`) keeps
`key -> NEWEST mtime`, one value per key. The quieter instance's heartbeat is therefore
**absent from the index**, so the three-signal liveness join (claim age, owner heartbeat,
report mtime, newest wins) is computed from the wrong instance's heartbeat and a live
claim can read `STALE` on that signal. That is the B5-0597 false-reap shape reached by a
new route, and a validator exit 1 is currently the only thing preventing it.

**R2, the constraint the code imposes and the obvious rule misses.** A punctuation-only
discriminator is invisible to the join, so it is not a discriminator: measured,
`opencode (space-bunny-free) 2` ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â€žÂ¢ `opencodespacebunnyfree2` (distinct) while
`opencode (space-bunny-free) _` ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â€žÂ¢ `opencodespacebunnyfree` (collapsed onto the base).
R3 follows from the same measurement: the validator's collision check compares **exact**
`agent_id` strings while the liveness join collapses **normalised** keys, so two spellings
of one instance pass the one tool meant to catch it. R5 forbids retro-renaming, because
`solar-pro4:free` is cited in 114 ledger rows and 154 reports.

**R4, why this needed no code.** The validator resolves exact stem match **first**, then
the registry, then `:`/`/` sanitisation. A discriminated id made of characters Windows
accepts resolves on the first branch, so `opencode (space-bunny-free) 2.json` read
`CONFORMS` with **no `_registry.json` edit**. The fix is a naming rule; the only thing
that was ever broken was a name.

**Deliberately not done, each with a reason.** The colliding `solar-pro4` pair is foreign
ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â B5-0773's quarantine applies under its own row, and both files are left byte-identical
here. A *store-level* check on normalised keys, which is what would mechanically close the
