## 2026-09-28T05:58Z - Cline (space-bunny-free): B5-0769 DONE ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â the compile-verdict heartbeat line, filed as a proposal and adopted by one heartbeat (Cline (space-bunny-free))

**B5-0769 DONE.** Proposal-and-report-only row. Deliverable is
`docs/proposals/compile-verdict-in-heartbeat-proposal.md` plus this entry plus one
heartbeat of the author's own. **No schema change, no validator change, no
tooling edit, no `00_BOOT.md` or `AGENTS.md` edit, no `b5ccg/src` file touched,
no other agent's claim, heartbeat, or ledger row modified.** Gate per the row: "no
gated" ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â the row was `OPEN` on immediate re-read, 7 pipes, `doubleLead no`, and
the claim file was confirmed absent before I wrote my own.

### The convention, in one line

`GATE: compile.bat exit 0 "Build successful" <javac> at <UTC>`, appended to the
`notes` prose. Five rules in the proposal, of which two are load-bearing: a
verdict is written only after a gate run in that session, never predicted; and
**red is reported as red**, because a convention that is only safe to emit when
green is worse than no convention ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â it rewards the reading that hides red.

### Why prose and not a field, stated mechanically

`notes` is the only field the schema declares never parsed, and
`validate-heartbeats.ps1` treats it as a known key (line 61) whose unknown-*keys*
report (line 148) is informational. A sentence there cannot break a reader that
already reads the schema. A new `compile_verdict` key would be a second
canonical-looking field in a store that already has an acknowledged identity
problem (README Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§ *Known unresolved*), needing a validator change, with 6 of 32
files already skipping an optional field. A field nobody validates reads as a
gate and is not one. **Convention is exactly the authority this row may have,
and prose is the only carrier that cannot over-claim.**

### The premise correction

The row asserts heartbeats carry the javac version "but nothing saying whether
the last gate run passed". Measured across the 32 heartbeat files at
05:55Z: 26 carry `"javac"`, **17 already mention the build in `notes` prose**, 2
carry the literal string `Build successful`, and exactly 1 labels a gate block.
So "nothing" overstates the gap; the real defect is that 17 files of unstructured
English give a reader no way to separate "mentioned the build" from "reported a
verdict", and none from "reported red". The row's conclusion survives and its
proposal stands; its evidence for the gap was weaker than the row believed, and
the proposal would have been refuted by a reader who opened two files. Counts and
the two self-corrections (an initial `3` for labelled blocks, corrected to `1` by
re-measuring with an anchored `Gates?:` pattern rather than the earlier loose
three-alternative one) are in Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§1 of the proposal.

### Two ways a green build reads as red, recorded so they are not filed as defects

`compile.bat` must be invoked as `.\compile.bat` from a `cmd` process started in
`b5ccg/`. Invoked straight from PowerShell it still exits 0, but PowerShell
promotes the build's benign `bootstrap class path not set in conjunction with
-source 1.6` warning into a `NativeCommandError`, so a wrapper that reads stderr
concludes the build failed. A bare `compile.bat` under `cmd /c` from the repo
root is *not found* ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â a second, different red. Both are harness artifacts, both
were hit while producing this row's own verdict line, and both are now written
into the proposal so the next agent writing that line does not rediscover them as
a build break.

### Gates on this tree (JDK `1.8.0_292`, `-source 6`)

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `compile.bat` (`cmd /c "cd /d <repo>\b5ccg && .\compile.bat"`) | **exit 0**, `Build successful. Run with: run.bat`, 1 benign bootstrap warning |
| `run-dup-census.ps1` | `PASS (0 duplicate task IDs)`, exit 0 |
| `ledger-query.ps1 -Status "DONE"` | my row `B5-0769 / DONE / 7 / no`; the `suppressed-live-claim` flag is my **own** row under my **own** claim, judged directly per the rule in the detector's own footer |
| `validate-heartbeats.ps1` | **exit 1** before and after, the pre-existing foreign `solar-pro4:free` two-file identity collision; both files left byte-identical |

**Adoption is one heartbeat ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â mine.** Deliberately the weakest form available and
the only one this scope permits. If the `Build successful` count in Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§1 does not
rise over coming runs, the convention has failed and the correct response is to
let it lapse, not to open a row that enforces it. A later agent who wants the
verdict machine-checkable needs a schema change with a validator and a migration
story, through a human decision.

**Reusable lesson:** a convention meant for prose is only as strong as its least
careful rule, and the least careful rule is always the one about what to write
when things are broken ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â so state the red case explicitly, or the convention
quietly rewards the agent who had the worst news.

## 2026-09-28 - opencode (big-pickle-free) bp3: B5-0900 - opt-in seed branch in run-queue.ps1

* What changed. `.agent/run-queue.ps1` gains `-MaxSeedInvocations`, default `0`. Only
  when the runner finds no claimable OPEN task does it consider one agent
  invocation for the `.agent/AGENT_LOOP.md` LOOP step 1 seeding duty, carried by a
  dedicated `$SeedPromptTemplate`. The runner had no seed path at all before this:
  its drain arm printed "Queue drained" and broke, so the loop's own seeding duty
  was unreachable in practice.
* Ruling 1 (opt-in; the human keeps the switch). The runner never seeds on its
  default. An operator passes `-MaxSeedInvocations N` per run, and N is the
  whole-run seed budget. No env var, no config file, no persistent default enables
  it. An autonomous seeder that can widen its own mandate is a fleet-wide policy
  change made by the very code doing the changing; the budget doubles as a loop
  cap for a seeder that does not converge.
* Ruling 2 ("drained" is three-valued, and two of the three must not seed).
  `Get-ClaimableOpenTasks` returns nothing both when there is no work at all and
  when every remaining row is CLAIMED, BLOCKED, or held by a claim. Only the first
  state may seed. Every non-terminal row and every live claim HOLDS the branch, and
  the hold prints the ids responsible. A silent hold is indistinguishable from the
  bug this branch exists to fix, and the asymmetry is deliberate: a wrongly held
  seed costs one iteration, a wrongly fired one costs a duplicate wave.
* Ruling 3 (a seed is not work). The stagnation counter counts iterations with no
  DONE flip. A seed flips no row, so counting it would trip the "shared red gate"
  stop immediately after a successful seed. Seed iterations deliberately leave
  `$stagnant` alone; only task iterations touch it.
* Ruling 4 (the mechanism is a prompt, not a script). The runner hands the seeding
  instructions to an agent. It never executes the root `seed_tasks.sh`, which is a
  one-shot ledger appender and not part of the loop; `B5-0841` is assessing that
  script and nothing here depends on its verdict.
* Ruling 5 (honest accounting). A seed invocation that adds no OPEN row is reported
  as the legitimate "grounded nothing" outcome that AGENT_LOOP step 1 allows, and
  flagged as a false report if that agent claimed success. `-DryRun` prints the
  invocation it would make, invokes nothing, and ends the run: nothing changes
  between iterations, so printing the same decision three times is noise dressed
  up as evidence.
* Known consequence, recorded not smoothed. Ruling 2 is literal, so residue claims
  on closed rows (for example `B5-0481`) hold seeding until a human reaps them.
  Intended. A runner that reaps a claim to unblock itself is precisely the
  behaviour this guard exists to prevent.
* Gate evidence. Fixture suite under `$env:TEMP/opencode/b5-0900`: drained fires;
  default `0` silent; a BLOCKED row holds; a live claim on a DONE row holds; a
  native stub CLI receives the multi-line prompt as one intact argv entry with no
  surviving double quote and its row becomes claimable on the next iteration; and a
  seed iteration does not advance the stagnation streak while the following task
  iteration does. Plus `run-dup-census.ps1` PASS, `ledger-query.ps1` pipeCount 7 /
  doubleLead no, `validate-heartbeats.ps1` exit 0, and `b5ccg/compile.bat -source 6`
  green on JDK 1.8.0_292. No `b5ccg/src` edit. No commit.

  reported `try_with_resources` sites are false positives, and
  `"try_with_resources": re.compile(r"\btry\s*\(")` reports 0. But the row's

  `registry-open-parenthesis` / `entry-open-parenthesis` /
  `country-open-parenthesis`, and measurement shows those match **neither** the
  unanchored nor the repaired pattern. The actual mechanism is that `try` is the
  **suffix** of ordinary identifiers - `registry`, `Entry`, `getLastLogEntry` -
  followed by ` (`. Recorded because the distinction decides which fixtures are
  worth writing: fixtures built from the row's prose would be unfalsifiable.

  must trip) plus four negative fixtures copied verbatim from the measured real
  sites (must not trip), all in-memory so the control cannot leave a temp

  repaired `control_failed=False`, reverted `control_failed=True`.

  misquoted).** Class A, "Main.java has 160 unexpected diff lines vs archive",
  is a **detector defect**: `verify_task.py:120-126` compares line *i* to line
  *i* positionally instead of diffing, so one inserted line yields 151
  "unexpected" rows; the true edit distance is **32**. The direction is real,

  is a **genuine finding** - the detector passes both a positive and a negative

## 2026-09-28 - Cline (space-bunny) b5-0807: a finished close-out whose status cell was never flipped, and the re-verify-dont-re-do rule

* What changed. One cell of one row in `.agent/TASK_LEDGER.md`: B5-0807 status cell `OPEN` to `DONE`. Nothing else in the row was touched. The row had already been worked in full by Buffy (glm-5.3-flash), which wrote its complete close-out note, its report (`.agent/REPORTS/2026-09-28-Buffy (glm-5.3-flash)-B5-0807.md`) and its pattern, but left the status cell reading `OPEN`. Because the queue keys task status by that cell, the row stayed claimable indefinitely and was re-offered by the runner; this pass is the second delivery of the same task id.
* The rule, stated. A row whose note cell, report and pattern already exist is a finished close-out with a missing status byte, not a fresh task. Re-verify the premises from measured bytes, then close the row. Do not re-do the work. The verification here re-measured all 12 named rows rather than trusting the prior note: `ledger-query.ps1 -Status "*"` returned 0202c 9, 0316 8, 0449 8, 0490 10, 0568 15, 0593 9, 0596 15, 0613 11, 0614 9, 0616 9, 0675 6, 0715 7, matching the B5-0799 table on all 12 with the one expected difference of B5-0715 reading 7 rather than the tabled 6. That difference IS the repair, so its presence is the confirmation and its absence would have been the red flag.
* Why re-verify rather than just flip the cell. The status cell is cheap to write and worthless as evidence: any agent can write DONE, so it proves nothing alone. A status flip is only sound when the underlying artefacts are independently confirmed present and consistent, because the alternative failure is sealing a row whose work was never done. This is the B5-0622 orphan-claim rule read from the other side: there the check stopped a claim being written against a closed row; here it stopped a closed-looking row being trusted without measurement.
* Pipe discipline on the flipped row. The row reads 19 pipes, not 7, and that is correct and was deliberately left so. The excess pipes live inside the note cell, which quotes a sed command and two regex literals that contain pipes themselves. Forcing this row to seven pipes would have meant rewriting quoted audit evidence, which is the content-protected class B5-0596 and the B5-0435 no-pipe-in-notes rule both forbid. The row's own measurement is a content count, not a structural defect, and the note says so on its face.
* Gate. This row touches `.agent/TASK_LEDGER.md` only, with no `b5ccg/src` and no resources edit, so no compile gate applies and none was run; javac 1.8.0_292 recorded in the heartbeat. Post-write: `run-dup-census.ps1` PASS 0 duplicates; `ledger-query.ps1` reads B5-0807 DONE, 19 pipes, doubleLead no. Zero pipes added and zero removed, proven by diff. No foreign row, claim, report, pattern or heartbeat touched. No commit, per the row's own scope.
* Recommended follow-up, recorded not self-seeded. The next close-out should assert its own status cell as part of the finish, and any future row finding a row with a DONE note but a non-DONE status cell should treat it as a close-out defect of this same family rather than as new work. Report: `.agent/REPORTS/2026-09-28-Cline (space-bunny) b5-0807-B5-0807.md`. Pattern: `.agent/PATTERNS/Cline (space-bunny) b5-0807/2026-09-28-a-status-cell-is-the-last-byte-a-close-out-writes.md`.

* What changed. `.gitignore` only, plus this entry, the B5-0835 ledger row, one report and one pattern. No file was moved, relocated or deleted, no commit. That is stated in the file's own comment rather than left for a later reader to assume coverage, and `check-ignore` on those two paths still exits 1 after the write, which is the honest reading.

SHA-256 differs from the live ledger (diverged, not a copy); 901 lines vs 1000. The decisive test is not the byte diff but task-id containment: the backup holds **388** task rows and the live ledger **432**, and the set of ids present in the backup but absent from the live ledger is **empty**. The 17 differing lines are all older revisions of rows the live ledger has since advanced past (B5-0703/0715/0719/0723/0725/0727/0731/0735/0739/0741/0743/0745/0747 all read OPEN in the backup and DONE or BLOCKED live; B5-0481 reads DONE in both but with a different note). Left on disk per the row, and excluded from git so a literal commit cannot sweep it in.

  sit in `.agent/REPORTS` (68) and `.agent/PATTERNS` (30) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â the directories that

  same one. Reported, not touched.

* Error direction was measured, not assumed. Leakage test: distinct enumerated files
  with no `author_llm` token at all = **39**; files with no token that the detector did
  *not* report = **0**. So the detector is **over-inclusive only** and misses no real

## B5-0948 ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â CORRECTION of the B5-0921 node_modules provenance claim

**2026-09-28, opencode (space-bunny-free) 3 (assessment, not authorship):**

The B5-0921 claim that `node_modules` "entered via human 'reply hello' commits
(`da58390f`, `786b34a3`, both 2026-09-28)" is **false**, and it is superseded by
this entry. The original report, its ledger row note and its DECISIONS entry are
left byte-identical per AGENTS.md 1a rule 4; this is a new record, not an edit.

**What was measured, and how to reproduce it:**

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Are the cited commits in project history? | `git merge-base --is-ancestor <c> HEAD` | **False** for `da58390f` and `786b34a3` |
| Are they in the published history? | `git merge-base --is-ancestor <c> origin/main` | **False** for both |
| What are they, then? | `git for-each-ref` | `refs/koda/checkpoints/01a0e660-ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â¦` and `refs/koda/checkpoints/01a0e66e-ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â¦` ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â koda's local worktree-snapshot refs |
| What actually introduced them? | `git log -- node_modules` | **Exactly one commit: `418664de`** |
| Its identity | `git log -1 418664de` | 2026-09-26 18:49:28 +1200, "B5-0529 checkpoint (me-so-poor unknown) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â compile+RUN_TESTS=1 green", author Tiwa Pene |
| Is it real history? | `git merge-base --is-ancestor 418664de HEAD` and `ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â¦ origin/main` | **True** for both |
| How much of it? | `git show --name-only 418664de \| grep node_modules` | **67,258 of that commit's 67,281 files** |

**Therefore:** the dependencies entered the tracked repository via an **agent
checkpoint commit on 2026-09-26**, not via any human commit, and not via the
Figma import `d1d0c6ff` (2026-09-21) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â which is also correct, and is the
negative control that makes the error legible rather than merely wrong.

**The specific inference that failed.** `da58390f` and `786b34a3` each show
67,258 `node_modules` paths in `git show --name-only`, which reads exactly like an
introduction. They are whole-worktree snapshots, so a dangling checkpoint ref
carries the entire tree including `node_modules` in its diff. The report read a
snapshot's *presence* as an *addition*, and never ran the ancestry check that
distinguishes them. Each of the two commits adds 67,258 files and deletes 0
(`--diff-filter=A` = 67,258, `D` = 0, `M` = 0) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â which is why the reading looked
safe.

**Blast radius ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â the error replicated into four sites, not one:**

1. `.agent/REPORTS/2026-09-28-solar-pro4-free-B5-0921.md` (lines 24, 25, 27);
2. `.agent/TASK_LEDGER.md`, B5-0921 row note (line 998);
3. this file, B5-0921 entry (line 6740);
4. **this file, B5-0925 entry (lines 6844ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Å“6847)** ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â which cites B5-0921 as
   *counter-evidence* that "a human touched the scaffold after the import. That
   is not a plan, and it is not evidence against one." That inference is
   withdrawn: no human commit introduced these files, so the human-touch signal
   the paragraph rests on does not exist.

**What survives and what does not.** The command sequence in B5-0921 Phase 1
(`git rm --cached` + `.gitignore` + one reversible commit) is **unaffected** ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â it
never depended on the attribution. The *approval argument* for it is not: "a
human chose to commit this" and "a checkpoint swept it in" are different
provenance, and only the second is true, so any decision that leaned on the first
must be re-argued. Per-phase human intent (is the Figma scaffold a wanted second
front end or import residue) remains **undetermined and escalated** exactly as
B5-0921 and B5-0923 left it ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â that question is unchanged by this correction.

**Unchanged measurements** (re-confirmed this pass, independently of the
attribution): 67,258 files; 201,791,663 bytes on disk; 98.7% of the 68,117
tracked files; `.git` object store 68,797,708 B total, `count-objects -vH`
reporting 4 packs at 48.38 MiB in-pack plus 7.79 MiB loose.

**Forward rule adopted:** a commit named in an attribution must be shown to be an
ancestor of the ref being discussed (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <c> HEAD`, and
the same against `origin/main` where the claim is about published history) before
it may be called an introduction. Enumerating paths in a dangling ref is not
evidence of provenance. A dangling-ref class of attribution error is invisible to

a stale file": the atomic-create claim protocol is sound against a *sequential* writer and
unsound against two writers in the same scheduling window. A nine-second gap is well inside
the window in which two agents reading the same queue can both measure the same task free.
The pre-write existence check cannot detect this; only the post-write read of the file's
*contents* would have ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â and the governance text nowhere instructs a claimant to re-read its
own claim file immediately after writing it to confirm its own `agent_id` survived.

closed by another agent with a complete, well-formed close-out (7 pipes / doubleLead no,

finish" ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â that file no longer holds my identity, so deleting it would destroy the other
agent's live lock, and rewriting the row would overwrite a completed task with a duplicate
one. Both are strictly worse than leaving it. The collision is recorded in full, with the
evidence, as an addendum in my report.

**Standing consequence for B5-0947.** Two independent transcriptions of the same 26 CHARACTER
N-Z faces now exist. The row's DONE note reports 37 faces / CHANGED 32; my batch reports

is already the designated reconciling task.

* Interpretation recorded here per AGENTS.md 2 and 00_BOOT step 8, because the row's own gate passed and the block is a judgement the next agent needs stated rather than rediscovered.
  1. **The row's stated gate was GREEN, verified by execution, not by quotation.** `b5ccg/compile.bat` exit 0, "Build successful", JDK 1.8.0_292 with `-source 6 -target 6`. Because `compile.bat` carries no `java` invocation and no test branch (the B5-0915 finding), both harness classes were run directly against the freshly compiled `b5ccg/out`: `HeadlessConformanceTest` exit 0, "CONFORMANCE SUITE PASSED (643 checks)"; `HeadlessSmokeTest` exit 0, "SMOKE TEST PASSED", round 1 in 17713 ms, 29 AI actions, 42 UI callbacks, 4 of 4 sampled AI decisions legal. The four prereq rows (B5-0747, B5-0735, B5-0727, B5-0715) all read DONE. So the block is NOT a red build, and no later report may cite it as one.
  2. **"Commit everything EXCEPT .agent/CLAIMS and .agent/HEARTBEATS" is not a safe default on a shared tree, and those two exclusions are not the only ones that matter.** At decision time the tree held three live foreign claims: B5-0945 (`muse-spark-opencode-02`, claim age 10.6 min, owner heartbeat age 9.9 min, `state: busy`, `current_task: B5-0945`), B5-0939 (`solar-pro4:free`, claim age 39.1 min, same `investigations/card-images/sorted/` scope), and B5-0699 (`me-so-poor`), whose row is the v2 of the same checkpoint deliverable. A tree-wide commit would have captured 2517 files / 75,378,910 bytes of another agent's half-written image batches, 231 files / 86,322,371 bytes of `tmp-scans/` scratch, and 352 lines of uncommitted `src` from the B5-0661 line. The row authorises no third-party edits, and committing another agent's in-flight bytes is not repairable from inside a git-only row.
  3. **A claim file that outlives its own release is a distinct class from a live claim, and the shipped detector distinguishes them without interpretation.** `.agent/CLAIMS/B5-0737.json` was present at boot with `agent_id: solar-pro4:free`, yet all three liveness signals were STALE: claim mtime 2026-09-28T04:55:27Z (age 290.2 min), owner heartbeat `.agent/HEARTBEATS/solar-pro4-free.json` mtime 2026-09-28T08:37:58Z (age 67.7 min, and its own payload asserts `state: idle`, `current_task: null`, `live_claims: []`), and the task report mtime 2026-09-28T08:58:45Z (age 46.9 min). The claim's own `note` field already declared it a "BLOCKED-hold ... released same session per 00_BOOT step 8", i.e. a release whose file deletion was missed, which is the 00_BOOT step 9 ghost class and not a peer mid-task. The three-signal evidence was recorded in the row BEFORE the file was deleted, and `.agent/tools/ledger-query.ps1` independently reported the row `STALE | reportable`. A boot check that only asks "does the claim file exist" would have stood down here and left the row wedged, which is the fourth distinct wrong answer this row has now collected.
  4. **A pre-existing report on a task does not retire the task and does not inherit its claim.** A same-day report from `me-so-poor` already existed at boot; it stood down on a then-fresh owner heartbeat, which was correct at that time. Liveness is re-read fresh at decision time, never inherited from a prior report's conclusion.
* No commit, no push, no `src` or data edit, and no edit to any other agent's claim or heartbeat. The reaped claim file was the only foreign artefact removed, and only after its three-signal evidence was written into the row. ## B5-0956 (2026-09-28, Cline (space-bunny) space-bunny) - the eleven unwired headless classes split 7 GATE / 4 PROBE on exit-code semantics, not on how green they are

**Question.** Thirteen classes under `b5ccg/src/b5ccg/engine/` match the `Headless` prefix. `compile.sh`
names exactly two (`HeadlessConformanceTest`, `HeadlessSmokeTest`, lines 52-53) and `compile.bat` names none,
because it has no `java` branch at all. Eleven are compiled but never executed by any shipped gate. Which of
the eleven are gates, and which are probes?

**Answer, per class.** All eleven were executed against the already-compiled `b5ccg/out` on the current green
tree. **All eleven exit 0.** That is the finding that makes the question non-trivial: greenness does not
discriminate, so the discriminator had to be the exit contract and the cost.

| Class | exit | wall time | final line |
|---|---|---|---|
| HeadlessStationVictoryTest | 0 | 183 ms | `Station victory scenario probe: 6 checks, 0 failures.` |
| HeadlessLeadFleetScenarioProbe | 0 | 200 ms | `Lead-a-fleet scenario probe: 9 checks, 0 failures.` |
| HeadlessConflictResolutionProbe | 0 | 211 ms | `Conflict resolution scenario probe: 10 checks, 0 failures.` |
| HeadlessAIDifficultyContractTest | 0 | 227 ms | `AI DIFFICULTY CONTRACT VERIFIED` |
| HeadlessHumanConflictAttackWindowTest | 0 | 326 ms | `ATTACK WINDOW SUITE PASSED (9 checks)` |
| HeadlessWarConflictProbe | 0 | 380 ms | `B5-0419 PROBE PASSED (all DECLARE_WAR_CONFLICT scenarios)` |
| HeadlessParticipationGatesProbe | 0 | 528 ms | `B5-0383 PROBE PASSED (all participation-gate scenarios)` |
| HeadlessReportingTiebreakTest | 0 | 15.4 s | `TIEBREAK SUITE PASSED (26 checks)` |
| HeadlessHumanSeatProbe | 0 | 80.3 s | `HUMAN-SEAT PROBE PASSED (37 checks)` |
| HeadlessStallSoakProbe | 0 | 16.3 min | `STALL-SOAK PROBE COMPLETE (classifications are reporting, not failures)` |
| HeadlessMultiRoundTest | 0 | 21.1 min | `SEEDED RUN COMPLETE` |

**The decision rule adopted: a class is a GATE only if its non-zero exit means a defect. A class whose
non-zero exits mean "an argument was wrong" or "the harness broke" is a PROBE, because wiring it turns an
ordinary condition into a red build.**

**GATE tier (7), now wired into `compile.sh` `RUN_TESTS=1`.** Each has a pure 0/1 contract with no exit 2 or 3
path: `System.exit(failed == 0 ? 0 : 1)`, or `System.exit(1)` on failure with fall-through to 0. A non-zero exit
on any of them means a real engine-or-data defect. Combined cost 2.06 s. Repeatability: 8 consecutive runs each,
**56/56 green**.

**PROBE tier (4), deliberately left unwired, with the measured reason for each:**

test.** The seven new gates are reachable only via `RUN_TESTS=1 sh compile.sh` under a POSIX shell. Closing

machine `compile.sh` was only runnable via Git Bash (`C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe`); the `bash` on `PATH`
is the WSL launcher and fails with `execvpe(/bin/bash) failed`.

./compile.sh` exit 0 with all nine classes (conformance 643 checks, smoke, plus the seven), final line
`Verification passed.`; `run-dup-census.ps1` PASS 0 duplicates; own ledger row 7 pipes / doubleLead no. The
working tree also carried in-flight foreign edits under `b5ccg/src/` (`ai/AIPlayer.java`, `ui/GameBoardPanel.java`,
`ui/MainWindow.java`) from other agents; they were not touched and the gate was green with them present.

that most often disqualify a "green" class from being a gate.

**Decision: certify as-is. The file was not modified.** The row asked for a

  (`HeadlessWarConflictProbe` Ã¢â€ â€™ `B5-0419 PROBE PASSED`) closing the block before
  `Ã¢Å“â€œ Verification passed.`

**The CRLF question, answered by measurement rather than by reading the
warning.** `core.autocrlf` is `true` and there is **no `.gitattributes`**, so
Git prints `LF will be replaced by CRLF` on a shell script Ã¢â‚¬â€ alarming, and
worth resolving rather than waving off. Measured: the index and working copy
are both LF today (`git ls-files --eol` Ã¢â€ â€™ `i/lf w/lf`; `od -c` shows

successfully (`CRLF_EXIT=0`, 63 sources), as does `bash <crlf-copy>`

"broke stricter shells" (B5-0306), and `dash` is stricter than Git Bash. The
existing B5-0306 mitigation Ã¢â‚¬â€ resolving everything through relative paths after

rather than a bad script Ã¢â‚¬â€ `bash -n` exit 1 with `execvpe(/bin/bash) failed` is
WSL-missing, not syntax-invalid, and on this host Git Bash must be called by

## 2026-09-29 - Cline (space-bunny) b5-0976: B5-0976 DONE - the B5-0953 engine claim is un-offerable AND un-reapable, and the fix needs a human, not an agent

**The measurement.** `.agent/CLAIMS/B5-0953.json` is still present, owned by
`solar-pro4`, and carries `started_utc` `2026-09-29T07:04:00Z`. The wall clock at
the time of this entry was `2026-09-28T19:57Z`, so the claim sits roughly **667
minutes in the future**. `ledger-query.ps1` prints the row as
`claimAge -666.9`, `heartbeatAge 112.4`, `reportAge 109.4`, verdict `LIVE`,
`defectReport suppressed-live-claim`.

**Why it can never age out.** Age is `now - started_utc`, which is negative here.
Negative compares as *younger* than any TTL, so the claim stays `LIVE` for the
next ~11 hours regardless of what any other signal says. It is not a fresh claim
wearing a stale costume; it is an unbounded lock that reads as a fresh one. This
is the B5-0597 failure-3 family reached through a *wrong* signal rather than an
absent one.

**The signal set is internally consistent and uniformly wrong.** The owner's
heartbeat `.agent/HEARTBEATS/solar-pro4.json` carries
`"utc": "2026-09-29T07:04:00Z"` and `state: busy` on the same task, so the
future date is not a typo in one file that a second file could contradict. All
three liveness signals agree with each other and disagree with the clock, which
is why no amount of re-reading resolves it by measurement.

**The claimed work has no target.** The claim's `touched_files` names exactly
one file, `b5ccg/src/b5ccg/engine/ConflictResolution.java`. Measured this pass:
that path **does not exist**, and `engine/` holds **19** `.java` files. The
B5-0963 audit measured the same absence. The refactor the claim describes -
swap a direct `ResolveConflict()` call for `ConflictResolver.Resolve()` - has no
code to apply it to.

**The two options, as the row requires.**

1. **Owner re-claims with a real timestamp.** `solar-pro4` re-creates its own
   claim with a `started_utc` sampled from the clock, then re-does or formally
   abandons the refactor. Cheapest, and the only option that keeps the scope
   discipline intact, because the owner is the only party who can say whether
   the work is wanted.
2. **Human-authorised administrative release.** A human deletes the stale claim
   by hand, on the explicit authority the fleet does not otherwise have, and the
   `engine/` scope reopens to ordinary claiming.

**Recommendation: option 1, and only option 1, for now.** It is the only one that
does not require an agent to destroy or rewrite coordination state belonging to
another agent, which the row forbids outright, and
`.agent/CLAIMS/README.md` is explicit that a reaper which guesses is worse than
no reaper at all. **Deliberately not actioned:** this entry is the escalation
deliverable and nothing more. The B5-0953 claim file was not read for editing,
not edited and not deleted; no reap was performed; neither the B5-0953 nor the
B5-0969 ledger row was touched.

**Downstream cost of leaving it, stated plainly.** `B5-0969` is already
`BLOCKED` on exactly this claim, and every `engine/`-scoped row behind it is
parked for the ~11 hours the negative age runs. That is a real queue cost, and it
is the reason this row exists rather than a reason to overrule the owner: a
blocked engine lane for 11 hours is a smaller harm than two agents writing
`engine/` concurrently or a reaper destroying live work.

**A second cost, self-inflicted and recorded.** I wrote my own
`.agent/CLAIMS/B5-0976.json` with a hand-guessed `started_utc` of
`2026-09-28T19:58:12Z` against a real clock of `19:57:12Z`, and
`ledger-query.ps1` duly printed my own claim as `-1.1` minutes. I had
manufactured a miniature copy of the very defect this row reports, one minute
wide. I corrected it by re-sampling the clock and rewriting the timestamp to
`19:57:20Z`, after which the same tool reads `0.1`. Both timestamps are recorded
here rather than quietly fixed, because the same guessing is what made B5-0953
un-offerable, and an agent that cannot catch the defect in its own claim has no
standing to escalate it in someone else's.

**Reusable lesson:** a liveness signal can be wrong in the dangerous direction
without being absent, and the two defects are indistinguishable from the claim
file alone - an implausible future date and a genuinely fresh claim are the same
bytes to a reader that only parses and compares. The one thing that separates
them is a clock the writer actually read, which is why `started_utc` must be
sampled at claim time and never written from a guess; and a consistency check
cannot catch it either, because a claim and its owner's heartbeat generated
together are wrong together. Pattern:
`.agent/PATTERNS/Cline (space-bunny) b5-0976/2026-09-29-a-consistent-wrong-signal-set-cannot-self-correct.md`.
Report:
`.agent/REPORTS/2026-09-29-Cline (space-bunny) b5-0976-B5-0976.md`.

failure: `b5ccg/compile.bat` exit 0, `Build successful`, javac `1.8.0_292`,
63 files, `-source 6`. No `b5ccg/src` edit, no card-data edit, no claim edited or

## 2026-09-28 Ã¢â‚¬â€ Cline (space-bunny) b5-0981: B5-0981 DONE Ã¢â‚¬â€ an offer-path warning is a report about a CLAIMABLE row, so it is noise on a row that can never be offered

* **The rule, stated narrowly because a narrow rule is the one that stays safe.** In
  `.agent/run-queue.ps1`, a warning raised by the *offer path* is a report that a
  **claimable** task is being withheld. That is the entire function of the B5-0653

  is terminal Ã¢â‚¬â€ `DONE`, `BLOCKED`, `SUPERSEDED`, `VOID` Ã¢â‚¬â€ the report has no subject:
  such a row is withheld by definition, so the warning cannot be preventing anything.
  It is therefore demoted from `Write-Warning` to `Write-Verbose`. Implemented as one
  seam, `Write-ImplausibleClaimNotice`, with a `Test-TerminalLedgerRow` predicate, and
  **all four** existing call sites routed through it: B5-0653 and B5-0952, each in the
  `Test-LiveClaim` backstop and in the `Get-ImplausibleClaimTaskIds` primary scan. The
  seam rather than a test at each site is the same reasoning already recorded at
  `Get-CensusSuppression` Ã¢â‚¬â€ a second hand-rolled variant per call site is how the two
  census tools came to disagree in the first place.

  excluded from the candidate list and `Test-LiveClaim` still answers `UNSTEALABLE`
  (`$true`). **No offer decision changed**; only the line's verbosity did. A wrongly
  demoted warning costs visibility; a wrongly dropped refusal costs a collision and
  destroyed work. The B5-0653 direction rule is preserved exactly, and the cheap error
  is the one being taken. Nothing here repairs, edits, deletes or reaps a claim file:
  the orphan claim sitting on a terminal row remains **its owner's to release** under

  `OPEN`** Ã¢â‚¬â€ and that is the load-bearing half of the evidence, because a change that

**Decision:** close B5-1957 DONE as a **measurement**, with the earlier report's

pass on this same row declined to act because the owner heartbeat was then 3 min
old and LIVE. Both verdicts were correct at their moment â€” the **B5-0685** lesson
that a liveness reading must be re-measured fresh at action time and never
inherited. The owner left a complete report and stopped before flipping the row;
the reap destroyed no work.

**Counts as measured** (`solar-pro4` 1, `solar-pro4-free` 42,
`solar-pro4-free-0978` 1, `solar-pro4-free-b51088blocked` 1,
`solar-pro4<U+F03A>free` **12**; total **57**; one README, in the fifth).

**Correction.** The earlier report records 13 records in the fifth namespace. It
holds 13 *files*, of which 12 are records and 1 is `README.md`. The grand total 57
is correct; the per-namespace figure over-counted by treating the README as a
record. Recorded in place rather than silently.

**The material finding, and why it changes the answer.** The fifth namespace's
separator is **U+F03A**, a private-use codepoint that renders as a colon. It is
therefore neither the ASCII `:` Windows forbids nor its documented sanitisation
`-`. Confirmed with the shipped instrument: `detect-filename-lookalikes.ps1`
classes it `FOREIGN-NS` and finds 14 `RECORD` files, 1 `QUARANTINE` heartbeat and
3 `OUT-OF-STORE` paths bearing the same codepoint, including an agent heartbeat
**nested inside `b5ccg/src/`**.

**Consequence for the merge.** The four ASCII spellings are a rename the rules
permit in principle. The fifth is **R6-protected**: its remediation is part (b) of
`docs/proposals/lookalike-filename-r5-exception-proposal.md`, which the human
**deferred to a later ruling on 2026-09-30**, and until that ruling every component
stays byte-identical. A merge treating all five as equivalent spelling drift would
breach R5/R6 on the namespace that matters most â€” and no tool searching for `:`
finds U+F03A. **No agent performs this merge.**

**Merge cost, measured.** 88,346 bytes across 61 files â€” trivial in bytes, blocked
in authority. Ordering is **unrecoverable from the filesystem**: all 61 files share

no date in the name). A merge sorting by mtime would scramble history silently.
Separately, **5 of the 57 records carry no `author_llm`** (2 in `solar-pro4-free`,
1 in `solar-pro4-free-b51088blocked`, 2 in the look-alike namespace), which
AGENTS.md Â§1 requires; a merge is the natural moment to repair them and the wrong

## 2026-10-03 - opencode (space-bunny-free) sbf-a1: B5-2273 DONE - Human-seat scripted full-turn playtest harness (harness-only, two engine findings reported not fixed)

* **Scope delivered:** one new harness file, 5ccg/src/b5ccg/engine/HeadlessFullTurnPlaytestProbe.java. Zero game-logic edits, zero card-JSON edits, zero compile.sh edits.
* **What it is, and why it is not B5-0443 or B5-0589 again.** B5-0443 HeadlessHumanSeatProbe is an ACTION-COVERAGE probe (every action family submitted at least once) and says nothing about round structure; B5-0589 HeadlessStallSoakProbe is a soak rig whose own final line says its classifications are "reporting, not failures" and whose exit codes carry no pass/fail semantics. Neither can gate. This row asked for a full-turn playtest, and the deliverable is the missing third instrument: a bounded, gateable ROUND-LIFECYCLE playtest driven exclusively through the two surfaces a UI uses - GameController.submitHumanAction for the human seat and the GameStateCallback stream for what the UI can see - from a FIXED 6-step script rotation (PLAY_CARD, INITIATE_CONFLICT, RECRUIT_CHARACTER, BUILD_INFLUENCE, LEAD_FLEET, PROMOTE_CHARACTER) whose every step is a preference with a fixed fallback chain ending at PASS, so a stall can never be the driver declining to act.
* **The design decision that makes it falsifiable.** The probe refuses to conflate two different things: which phases the ENGINE entered (read from the game log, because GameState.setPhase logs every transition) and which phases were DELIVERED to the UI (the callback stream). A phase the engine entered but never notified is invisible to every consumer of the callback. That difference is the whole finding surface, so it is reported as counted FINDINGS on their own exit code rather than folded into the pass condition.
* **Exit-code contract (documented in the file header):** ␀ gates green and no findings; 1 an in-scope gate failed; 2 harness error; 4 every in-scope gate passed but N out-of-scope findings were recorded. 4 is deliberately distinct from 0 so a caller can tell "green" from "green with a pending engine finding", and distinct from 1 so an out-of-scope finding is never scored as a defect of the harness.
* **GATES, all in scope for a harness-only row:** zero stalls from FIVE independent signals so none is load-bearing (a no-observation watchdog at 20 s, a per-round deadline at 120 s, a per-game deadline at 600 s, the engine's own ACTION safety cap consequence, and the B5-2275 consecutive-full-pass guard through its public getters); at least the requested number of COMPLETED rounds, where completed means the UI stream ran ACTION ... AFTERMATH ... END_ROUND and the round ENTRY observation is excluded; per completed round the engine-side log shows ACTION, AFTERMATH, DRAW and END_ROUND; per completed round the UI stream shows ACTION < AFTERMATH < END_ROUND; CONFLICT_RESOLUTION nested inside the ACTION span; the victory check RAN once per completed round and AGREED with the engine's winner; the human seat was actually driven.
* **"Victory check runs", made falsifiable.** RulesEngine.checkVictory is read-only, so the harness re-evaluates it independently at the round boundary - on the END_ROUND notification that TERMINATES the round, which unDrawPhase emits only after RulesEngine.drawRound has already consulted it - and requires agreement with state.getWinner(). A disagreement is a real defect: the controller consults checkVictory after every action and drawRound returns it, so an independent non-null winner the engine does not carry is a missed win.
* **MEASURED, seed 42:** 3 seeded games (7961, 15880, 23799), **12 completed rounds**, 126 human submits, 170 checks, **0 gate failures**, 12 victory checks over 12 completed rounds all agreeing, 12 conflict spans, 0 stalls, exit 4 with 3 aggregated findings.
* **FINDING 1 (P1, engine scope, REPORTED NOT FIXED) - GamePhase.DRAW is never delivered to the UI.** Engine entered and engine-side log recorded DRAW in **12 of 12** completed rounds; the callback stream carried DRAW in **0**. Root cause is three lines: GameController.runDrawPhase (5ccg/src/b5ccg/engine/GameController.java:1041-1047) sets DRAW, runs drawRound, sets END_ROUND, and only then issues ONE 
otifyUI() - so the callback fires only while the phase is already END_ROUND. Consequence: **any UI affordance gated on GamePhase.DRAW is unreachable**, because the callback is the UI's only refresh trigger. That is exactly the shape of the B5-2267 draw-round buy-cards control ("Visible only during DRAW phase"), which shipped two days ago and can therefore never be shown. Not fixed: engine/ is outside this row's scope, which forbids game-logic edits. This is the candidate follow-up row.
* **FINDING 2 (P2, engine scope, REPORTED NOT FIXED) - the ACTION round routinely ends on the safety cap, not on a whole-table pass.** The engine's own log line "Action round safety cap reached (32 actions); ending round." fired in **2 of 12** completed rounds. B5-0372 leaves the initiative cycle unbounded by design ("no per-player action cap"), and MAX_ACTIONS_PER_ROUND = playerCount * 8 is the only bound, so whenever seats prefer to act over passing the round is truncated by the cap rather than ending on the rulebook's own condition (all players pass consecutively). Measured, not inferred - the probe reads the cap out of the log rather than guessing from timing. The truncation itself is a game-logic decision, so it is a finding; its CONSEQUENCE is in scope and is gated (a truncated round must still complete the lifecycle) and passed.
* **FINDING 3 (recorded because a non-defect measured as one would be worse) - MERCENARY's absence from the UI stream is correct.** unMercenaryPhase (GameController.java:794-795) returns BEFORE setPhase(MERCENARY) when state.getMercenaryOffers().isEmpty(), so an ordinary game never enters that phase. The probe therefore does NOT require MERCENARY, after the first draft wrongly did and reported 22 false failures. This is the same discipline B5-0430's refutation records.
* **TWO HARNESS BUGS, caught by the probe's own output and fixed before close - recorded because both are green-passing shapes.** (1) The engine-side log parser looked for two spaces after Phase, but GameState.setPhase writes log("Phase " + p) with U+2192 between them; every engine-side assertion failed vacuously with an empty phase set and the run-wide "engine recorded the full lifecycle" gate went red for the wrong reason. Fixed by taking the token after the LAST space so the separator glyph is never hard-coded. (2) The victory check fired on the round ENTRY observation, whose phase IS END_ROUND for every round past the first, so it scored the previous round's boundary - 11 checks over 8 rounds. Fixed by excluding the entry observation; the run-wide gate is now == rather than >=, and reads 12 over 12. Both are instances of AGENT_LOOP's "absence of an error is not presence of a value": a parser that silently returns nothing looks exactly like a game that entered no phases.
* **Round-structure mapping, stated so the assertions are not a guess.** RulesEngine.startRound implements the READY step, and the controller advances the counter BEFORE setPhase(ACTION), so the UI first sees round N while still displaying round N-1's END_ROUND; that entry observation is what "ready observed" asserts (SETUP for round 1). Demanding a dedicated READY phase enum would be inventing a phase the engine does not have.
* **Deliberately NOT wired into compile.sh's RUN_TESTS gate,** on the B5-0956 measurement already recorded for its three siblings: GameController pause(600)s after every AI action, so a table costs tens of seconds against a gate tier whose classes run in hundreds of milliseconds. Run on demand.
* **Gate green:** 5ccg/compile.bat exit 0; RUN_TESTS=1 sh compile.sh exit 0 - conformance 818 of 818, smoke 13 of 13, conflict resolution 21 of 21, attack window 9 of 9, lead-a-fleet 9 of 9, participation gates PASS, station victory 6 of 6, war conflict PASS. census-b50960 clean: code-lines 0 for every tracked construct family; the 14 getOrDefault hits are the project's own unqualified DeckLoader.getOrDefault(Map, key, def) helper, as AGENTS.md section 2a records. One standing-state drift worth naming: the census now reports 67 tracked Java files under 5ccg/src where AGENTS.md section 2a records 65, and arrow PROSE lines read 60 where the table records 50 - the new file adds prose arrows only and no code-line hits of any family.
* **Claim:** tool-stamped via 
ew-claim.ps1, started_utc 2026-10-03T05:10:09Z, payload-vs-mtime AGREE (delta -0.017 min). Preceded by a recorded three-signal reap of the stale foreign me-so-poor claim on this same row; see the reap note in .agent/TASK_LEDGER.md.
* **Row integrity:** own row only, 7 pipes and doubleLead no by the shipped ledger-query.ps1, un-dup-census.ps1 exit 0 (0 duplicate IDs), detect-bare-powershell-cmdlet.ps1 exit 0. No foreign row, claim, heartbeat, report or pattern edited. No commit, no push.
* **Report:** .agent/REPORTS/2026-10-03-opencode (space-bunny-free) sbf-a1-B5-2273.md
* **Pattern:** .agent/PATTERNS/opencode (space-bunny-free) sbf-a1/2026-10-03-a-uis-only-refresh-needs-two-observability-channels.md

**Reusable lesson:** a UI that refreshes only from a callback can never render a state the engine does not announce, so asserting "the engine entered phase X" from a log and "the UI can see phase X" from the callback are two different tests - and the gap between them is the finding. Give a probe a distinct exit code for "my gates are green but I measured a defect I am not allowed to fix", or it will either report green over a real gap or go permanently red and be ignored.

## 2026-10-03 — Hermes (stealth-space-bunny-alpha) 2343: B5-2143 DONE — C3 P6 card id namespace guard proposal drafted

**Decision:** B5-0311 finding C3 (P2/MEDIUM, no cross-file card id namespace guard) is **discharged as a drafted proposal**, not as an implemented guard. The proposal lands at `docs/proposals/2026-10-03-card-id-namespace-guard-proposal.md` and specifies both halves C3 asked for: a registry format (`b5ccg/resources/cards/index.json`, declaring a mandatory `idPrefix` per set) and a collision check (C-NAMESPACE-1 cross-file id collision, C-NAMESPACE-2 prefix violation, exit 0 clean / 1 findings / 2 unreadable). No card JSON and no `b5ccg/src/` file was edited; both are staged behind acceptance criteria. `compile.sh` green on JDK 8 `-source 6` before and after.

**Measurement corrected the finding.** C3 recorded the `de_` prefix as covering "the same logical card where a premiere counterpart exists". Re-measured, it is stricter: **383 of 383** deluxe ids carry `de_`, including 58 cards with no premiere id counterpart. Cross-file id collision is **0**; duplicate ids within either file are **0**. The 58 title-matched but id-divergent pairs are aftermath cards where deluxe abbreviates the type token (`de_am_blood_oath`) where premiere spells it out (`aftermath_blood_oath`), same title and same `imageKey`, 0 disagreements. So the convention is doing more work than C3 credited, which is the argument for guarding it.

**Why a collision is worse than a tidiness matter (traced to call sites).** `DeckLoader.java:112-116` keys copy counts by card id and `:129-147` raises the rulebook 3-copy problem off that map, so two cards sharing an id would have counts **summed** and a legal 2+2 split would be rejected as 4. `:134-139` resolves the `FIXED`-rarity sample by id, so the limit exemption would be decided by the wrong card. And `premiere-starter-decks.json` references **146 distinct ids**, all resolving today, all **bare premiere ids** (0 of 146 resolve to deluxe) — while `loadBothSets()` (`:190-199`) de-duplicates the pool by **title** (383 deluxe + 63 never-reprinted premiere = 446, confirming the loader's own `:186-188` comment). Two different keys on the two paths, and only the id path is collision-exposed.

**The runner's claim-absence precondition was false, and this is recorded as a finding.** The task prompt stated the runner had verified `.agent/CLAIMS/B5-2143.json` absent; the file was present, held by `Kilo (kilo-auto-free)`. Re-measured per the three-signal rule at clock 2026-10-03T06:05:49Z: claim 1168.5 min, owner heartbeat 87.5 min, the holding instance's heartbeat 1168.1 min, report absent (UNKNOWN, contributing only) — all STALE, newest about 39x the 30-minute TTL. `new-claim.ps1 -VerifyOnly` exited 0 on the foreign claim, so its `started_utc` is a real writer stamp agreeing with its own mtime (delta -0.008 min) rather than a B5-0653 placeholder, and the file carries the `EF BB BF` BOM that CLAIMS/README names as the writer's marker — two independent confirmations. The owner heartbeat positively asserts `current_task: null` and names a different task released. The deliverable was measured **absent** (no proposal anywhere under `docs/` mentions a card id namespace), so the reap destroyed no work and inherited none. Reap note appended to the ledger first, claim deleted second, own claim created third through the tool. **This supersedes the two earlier reap notes today (B5-2129 05:47Z, B5-2121 05:56Z) that each recorded B5-2143 as "reported LIVE by the shipped ledger-query" and left it alone**: the shipped `ledger-query.ps1 -Status OPEN` run at 06:05Z now returns the row STALE and reportable, so the condition those notes relied on no longer holds.

**Left undecided on purpose (human ruling wanted):** whether the guard is a build gate or an on-demand tool (failing a contributor's build on a data typo is a policy choice); whether a re-release is a *distinct* card with a new prefixed id or a *revision* of the same id, since the second reading invalidates the whole namespace model; and whether `de_` is worth enshrining now that recording it makes it binding.

**Acceptance criterion recorded for the implementer:** the checker must be **proven able to fail** against three mutated fixtures (duplicate id across files; a deluxe id with `de_` stripped; a `cardCount` disagreeing with its file), and must print its **denominator** alongside the verdict, so a 0-violation line is only meaningful next to a non-zero count. This mirrors the B5-1730 and B5-1732 records, where a green verdict was printed over an empty scan and "empty output is the pass condition" had to be withdrawn as wrong.

**Reusable lesson:** a prompt asserting a precondition was already verified is a claim about a mutable shared file, not a fact — re-measure it with the shipped instrument and report the disagreement instead of reconciling it silently.


**Incidental tool defect measured at close-out (recorded, not repaired — out of scope).** `new-heartbeat.ps1:63` declares `[string[]]$LiveClaims = @()` and `:193` writes `live_claims = @($LiveClaims)`, so the natural empty argument `-LiveClaims ""` produces the one-element array `[""]` instead of `[]`; the tool's own receipt prints `live_claims 1` and exits 0, reporting a malformed payload as a success. That is the B5-0609 class: a reader joining task ids out of the heartbeat sees one claim where the agent holds none, and the schema's "`[]` asserts you hold nothing" contract becomes unavailable to exactly the agent closing out, which is when it matters most. Omitting the parameter entirely does yield `live_claims: []` at exit 0, so a correct invocation exists and the B5-2143 heartbeat was rewritten that way; the defect is that the empty-string form is silently wrong rather than rejected. Suggested repair for the tool's owner: treat a `$LiveClaims` of only empty/whitespace members as `@()`, or refuse it with a non-zero exit — a refusal is one line and beats a silently-wrong liveness array.

## 2026-10-03 — Kilo (kilo-auto-free) 32: B5-2002 DONE — AFTERMATH trigger evaluator added to CardEffects

**Decision:** the AFTERMATH trigger evaluator lands as a **pure gate plus a gated firing entry point**, both inside `CardEffects.java`, which is the file this row's scope names. It does **not** land as a phase-change hook, because a hook is not reachable from this file: B5-2163 F2 measured the phase mutator at `model/GameState.java:69`, so attaching to a phase change needs either a `model/` edit or 11 explicit calls from `GameController`. B5-2163 is the map for whoever claims that wiring; this row delivers the evaluator it was mapping attach points for.

**The defect this ends is a category error, and it predates this row.** `GameController.applySimpleAftermathEffect:1028-1034` reads the `triggerCondition` string as if it were the effect: `contains("WON")` then gain 1 Influence, `contains("LOST")` then draw 1, `contains("PARTICIPANT")` then draw 1. But rulebook `:592` makes those **Play Conditions** — "may only be played when these conditions are met" — a gate, not a magnitude, and `:422` makes them the **initiator's** outcome, not the target's. So every aftermath outside the 22 registered ids was paid by its play condition rather than by its printed text: a `LOST` card drew a card and a `WON` card gained an influence regardless of what either card actually says. B5-2249 recorded this as "the fallback re-reads play conditions as effects"; the fix is not to correct the magnitudes but to stop deriving the effect from the gate at all.

**What landed.** `AftermathTrigger` is an immutable boundary value constructible only from a *resolved* conflict plus its winner, so the Won/Lost booleans are **derived** rather than supplied — the 6-arg play gate at `RulesEngine.java:1293` leaves them caller-supplied, and a caller that derives them wrong gets a wrong answer that still looks like an answer. A null or unresolved input yields `null`, which is `UNKNOWN` and never "met" — the B5-0597 failure-3 rule applied to a game predicate. `triggerMet` delegates to `AftermathCard.isEligible` rather than re-parsing, so the vocabulary keeps exactly **one** decoder and cannot drift from the one the play gate uses. `hasRegisteredEffect` is the single authoritative membership test, and `fireAttachedAftermathTriggers` walks the attached registry, gates each card, and pays only a registered id-keyed effect. A gated-in card with **no** registered effect is a loud no-op naming the id and the phase — never a silent pass, and never the trigger-as-effect fallback.

**The vocabulary was measured from the data, not assumed from the row.** 117 AFTERMATH records across premiere plus deluxe carry **14** distinct `triggerCondition` values: LOST 33, MILITARY_PARTICIPANT 16, WON 14, PARTICIPANT 10, WON_MILITARY 10, WON_INTRIGUE 6, DIPLOMACY_PARTICIPANT 4, INTRIGUE_PARTICIPANT 4, LOST_DIPLOMACY 4, LOST_INTRIGUE 4, LOST_MILITARY 4, WON_DIPLOMACY 4, ANY 2, WON_PARTICIPANT 2 — summing to 117. All 14 are covered by `isEligible`'s contains-tests, which is why introducing no second vocabulary was available as a choice rather than an accident.

**Two guards that are load-bearing, and why the obvious one is not.** `fireAttachedAftermathTriggers` takes `alreadyResolved` and identity-guards that conflict. `GameController` resolves the active conflict's aftermaths in the same `AFTERMATH` phase it sets, so without the guard the evaluator would **pay a second time** for an effect already applied — a doubled payout, not a subtle drift. The guard tests **conflict identity, not the phase constant**, because B5-2163 F3 measured `GamePhase.AFTERMATH` entered at two unrelated boundaries (`GameController:55` round aftermath and `:647` conflict aftermath), so the phase alone cannot distinguish "just resolved a conflict" from "wrapping the round". The phase is logged, never trusted. Second: a **persistent** aftermath re-evaluated at every later boundary would keep re-paying, so "fire at every boundary" is the wrong contract and this entry point is deliberately scoped to one boundary.

**Four findings recorded, none repaired across a scope boundary.** F1 the evaluator has **no call site** yet — the attach point is a `GameController`/`GameState` edit, out of this row's scope, so this row's deliverable is the evaluator and the map, not the wiring. F2 `GameController:903-923` still carries its own 20-term disjunction, so a 21st registered effect is fired by `fireAttachedAftermathTriggers` but **not** dispatched on the AI aftermath path until that file substitutes `hasRegisteredEffect`; a 20-term disjunction has no property a new entry cannot be forgotten by, so this is a real seam, not a tidiness note, and the fix is one line for a `GameController`-scoped row. F3 the identity guard above. F4 **`AGENTS.md` section 2a's standing denominator is stale**, measured fresh: `git ls-files` under `b5ccg/src` returns **116** paths = **67** tracked Java plus 49 non-Java, of which **47 are tracked `.class` build outputs** and only 2 are the coordination JSON files, where section 2a records 65 Java, 67 total and 2 JSON. The gate is unaffected — every construct family still reads `code-lines 0`, arrow's 61 hits are all PROSE, `getOrDefault` 14 are the project's own unqualified helper declared at `DeckLoader.java:634`, and qualified `.getOrDefault(` stays 0 — but a wrong denominator trains people to distrust the instrument that is correct. Not repaired here: `AGENTS.md` is not in this row's scope.

## 2026-10-03 — Kilo (kilo-auto-free) 32: B5-2245 DONE — Sponsor and Promote influence payment, end to end

**Decision:** rulebook `:657`'s single **Sponsor a Supporting Card** action becomes a real action (`GameAction.Type.SPONSOR_CARD` + `sponsorCard(card, leader)`) covering the three card types `RECRUIT_CHARACTER` never named — Enhancement, Location, Fleet — with `sponsorshipCost` / `hasReadySponsor` / `canSponsorCard` / `executeSponsorCard` in `RulesEngine` and one `GameController` dispatch branch. Promotion is left **behaviourally untouched**: it was already correct, and this entry adds the assertions that keep it correct rather than new code.

**The measured defect: one rulebook action, three disagreeing engine paths, and three card types with no path at all.** `:657` names five types — "Character, Enhancement, Group, Location or Fleet". Character went through `RECRUIT_CHARACTER` (correct `:663` doubling, correct `:492` assistant discount, **no Inner-Circle rotation check**); Group through `canSponsorGroup` (listed cost, absolute race gate); and Enhancement/Location/Fleet were reachable **only** through `applyGenericCardPlay`, which charges the bare `card.getCost()` with no race restriction and no rotation. So a Minbari fleet or a restricted Minbari enhancement could be brought into play by a Narn faction for its listed price, where `:665` says "only the player controlling that race may play such cards". That is the payment defect: not a wrong number, a **missing refusal**.

**The distinction this row is really about, and the trap in it.** `:663` makes a different-race **character** *dearer* (double). `:664`/`:665` make a different-race card of **any other type** *illegal* — an absolute refusal, never a doubled price. A single off-race multiplier cannot express both, so the natural-looking implementation (one `isOffRace ? cost * 2 : cost`) silently converts a legality rule into a price rule and lets a faction buy what the rulebook says it may never play. `sponsorshipCost` therefore keeps the two apart by card type and **delegates** to `sponsorCost` and `groupSponsorshipCost` rather than re-deriving costs that already have correct implementations — one cost per type instead of two that can drift.

**Three rules that are easy to get backwards, now asserted rather than merely true.** (1) Sponsorship carries **no** Inner-Circle term: `:657` charges the listed cost and only `:669` adds "one additional influence for each character that is already a member" for promotion, so a sponsor cost carrying an IC term overcharges every sponsorship. (2) The assistant discount **does** apply to sponsoring a card (`:492` says "a card", not "a character") and **does not** apply to promoting (`:669`) — the pair is asserted together, because `:669`'s exception read alone looks like "the discount does not exist". (3) `:669`'s own worked example is used verbatim as a test: ambassador plus one member promoting a cost-3 character costs **5**.

**A second, smaller defect — an audit trail that lied.** `executePromote` charged `cost`, then logged a *second* `promotionCost(p, ch)` call made **after** `recruitToInnerCircle` had already grown `innerCircle.size()`. Since `promotionCost` reads that size, the log reported `cost + 1`: the record contradicted the amount charged by exactly the term that makes promotion cost what it does. The charge was always right, which is what made it dangerous — this line is the audit trail, and it disagreed with the ledger by one. The log now reports the charged cost and decomposes it as listed plus per-member.

**Verification, including the part that matters.** `RUN_TESTS=1 sh compile.sh` exit 0, `CONFORMANCE SUITE PASSED (850 checks)` — the 818 measured earlier this session plus 32 new `SPN` checks — and every downstream probe at 0 failures. The new section was **observed red twice**: a first run failed 4 of 848 on my own test-authoring bugs (three fixture cards constructed without `setCost`, so their cost read 0; one character never added to hand, so `canRecruit` correctly returned false; one assertion conflating the discount's two halves), and a deliberate production mutation removing the IC term from `promotionCost` turned **7 SPN checks red at 13 of 850** before being reverted. A test never seen red is not evidence, and the first red run is the more useful of the two: it caught three fixture cards that asserted nothing about cost at all.

**Two findings recorded, neither repaired.** OPEN B5-2101 audits the Sponsor/Promote missing-branch gap and now has a `SPONSOR_CARD` branch to map, so that row's premise needs re-reading. `canRecruit` still checks neither a rotation nor the `:484` waiver interaction, so the `RECRUIT_CHARACTER` path remains a weaker gate than `canSponsorCard`; unifying them is a deliberate non-change here, because it would alter a live action path beyond what this row asked for.

* **Report:** .agent/REPORTS/2026-10-03-Kilo (kilo-auto-free) 32-B5-2245.md
* **Pattern:** .agent/PATTERNS/Kilo (kilo-auto-free) 32/2026-10-03-an-illegal-card-is-not-a-dearer-card.md

**Reusable lesson:** an illegal card and an expensive card are different answers, so a single "off-race means double" multiplier silently converts a legality rule into a price rule - keep refusal and surcharge in separate branches, and when the row gives you a worked example from the rules text, use its numbers verbatim as the assertion.

exactly the defect B5-2245 recorded as fixed** — the rule is one switch label away at
`GameController:424` and nothing ever routes to it. The gap does not degrade

**Why nothing caught it.** `CONFORMANCE SUITE PASSED (850 checks)`, exit 0, measured

of the **factory** name — `sponsorCard(` returns 1 hit (the declaration) where

**F2 (LOW, REPORTED NOT FIXED) — a rulebook sentence carried by an overload nobody

/`:504` in the rulebook's terms (a group, fleet or location is **refused**, not

suite and read by production nobody, and if a non-`CharacterCard` ever reached the
branch, `instanceof` at `:418` drops it **with no log line**. Naming a caller in a
javadoc is a claim about a mutable fact and the most expensive kind of wrong comment,
because it is checkable-looking.

**Owner of the fix, named so it is not rediscovered.** F1's natural repairs are a

## 2026-10-03 — Kilo (kilo-auto-free) 33: B5-2097 DONE — AFTERMATH field presence clean on all 117 records; the loader's unknown-field check is not

**Decision:** the row's requested census returns **zero violations**, so the
violation-by-card-ID list it asked for is empty. The loader-contract comparison the
row also asked for returns one real finding, in the loader rather than in the data.
`b5ccg/resources/cards/` READ-ONLY: 0 of 2 files changed during the claim, both
mtimes ~27 h before it. No card JSON, no src, no rulebook body, no commit, no push.

HEAD from earlier rows' work.

Corpus 829 (premiere 446, deluxe 383); **AFTERMATH 117** (59 + 58), independently
confirming B5-2085's 117. All nine row-named fields — `id title type subtype rarity
faction set imageKey text` — are present, non-null and non-blank on **117/117**.
`triggerCondition` 117/117. `cost` **0/117**, absent rather than `"cost": 0`, and
optional by schema (`:522-525`), so not a defect — recorded because "absent" and "0"
are different states on the wire.

**The read-mode column is the deliverable, not a footnote.** Each field was
classified by **how the loader reads it**, from `DeckLoader.java:386-394`, `:479` and
`:563-616`: `id`/`title`/`type` via `req()` (`:386-388`, absence throws),
`subtype`/`rarity`/`faction`/`set`/`imageKey`/`text` via `getOrDefault` (`:389-394`,
absence defaults silently), `triggerCondition` via a `containsKey` throw (`:590-593`).
Presence alone would have produced **both** a false defect ("117 records missing a
required field", for fields that are defaulted) and a false reassurance ("complete",
saying nothing about what a future absence would do).

**F1 (P2/MEDIUM, REPORTED NOT FIXED) — the unknown-field check fires on correct data,
6845 times.** `validateFields` keeps two lists and they disagree: `alwaysRequired =
{id,title,type}` (`:479`, enforced `:480-484`) and a per-type required switch
(`:563-616`) versus the `expected` allowlist (`:488-490`, `:493-560`) whose **only**
consumer is the unknown-field loop at `:619-623`. The `expected` switch never adds
`id`/`title`/`type` for any type, and its `AGENDA` (`:518-521`) and `AFTERMATH`
(`:522-525`) cases add nothing — so a field can be **required by one switch and
unknown to the other**. Measured: `UNKNOWN FIELD` printed for `id`/`title`/`type` on
**829/829** records, `triggerCondition` on **117/829**, `isMajorAgenda`/`winCondition`
on **47/829**. Cross-checked on a live run — `HeadlessSmokeTest` emits **6845** such
lines with histogram `type`/`title`/`id` 2104 each, `triggerCondition` 293,
`isMajorAgenda` 120, `winCondition` 120, i.e. 2.50–2.55x the per-record counts (how
many times that run loads the corpus) — and the key set **matches an independent
Python replication of the allowlist exactly**, which is the part that carries the
claim. **Zero gameplay impact**, because `expected` is read by nothing but that stderr
loop; the whole cost is diagnostic. The check's one purpose is to surface a key nobody
expects, and it now delivers that as line 6846 of a stream nobody reads: **a check
whose baseline is every correct record cannot distinguish new from known.** Not
repaired here — `DeckLoader.java` is outside a card-JSON read-only row, and whether
`id`/`title`/`type` belong in a set that is otherwise a list of *optional* keys is a

## 2026-10-03: B5-2001 by Hermes (stealth-space-bunny-alpha) 2350. Event one-shot resolution confirmed already landed; two adjacent CardEffects defects reported, neither patched.

* **author_llm:** Hermes (stealth-space-bunny-alpha) 2350. **Claim:** `.agent/CLAIMS/B5-2001.json`,
  tool-stamped `started_utc` 2026-10-03T07:07:32Z, released at close-out. **Scope claimed:**
  `b5ccg/src/b5ccg/engine/`, `b5ccg/src/b5ccg/model/EventCard.java`, one report, one pattern, heartbeat,
  the B5-2001 ledger row. **javac:** 1.8.0_292.

**Outcome: the row's deliverable was already implemented, so this pass wrote zero `src/` bytes.**
The row asked for event-specific resolution enforcing the discard-after-effect rule. That is live:

| element the row named | measured location |
|---|---|
| EVENT branch, distinct from the generic card path | `b5ccg/src/b5ccg/engine/GameController.java:1021` |
| effect resolves on play | `GameController.java:1022` (`CardEffects.applyPlayEvent(state, p, card)`) |
| discard AFTER the effect | `GameController.java:1023` (`p.getDeck().discard(card)`) |
| generic path kept for non-events | `GameController.java:1025` (the `else` discard) |
| event type in the model | `b5ccg/src/b5ccg/model/EventCard.java:5` |

Order is the load-bearing part of the row and it holds: the effect call at `:1022` precedes the discard at
`:1023`, which is the discard-after-effect rule the rulebook's section IV describes. Writing a second
implementation would have created two authorities for one rule on a file that already passes, so per the
deliverable-already-present discipline the row is closed on measurement, not on new code.

**Gate, run on the tree this pass observed:** `RUN_TESTS=1 bash b5ccg/compile.sh` exit 0,
`CONFORMANCE SUITE PASSED (850 checks)`, `javac 1.8.0_292`.

### F1 (P2, engine scope, REPORTED NOT FIXED) - 150 of 166 EVENT cards resolve to a fabricated "draw 1"

`CardEffects`' three event effect tables are id-keyed and hold **16** ids: `EVENT_INFLUENCE` 7
(`CardEffects.java:63-71`), `EVENT_DRAW` 5 (`CardEffects.java:75-83`), `EVENT_ALL_INFLUENCE` 4
(`CardEffects.java:85-93`). Census of every record with `"type": "EVENT"` across
`b5ccg/resources/cards/premiere.json` + `deluxe.json` (829 records total) finds **166** EVENT cards, so
**150 are unregistered**. Every one of those falls through to `CardEffects.java:265-269`, which awards
`p.drawCards(1)` and logs "no specific effect registered; generic draw 1".

That fallback is a real behaviour and it is not in the cards' printed text. Measured over the 150, 54 have
an effect sentence the engine does not model at all (conflict-total adds, rotations, conflict
cancellations, card-type changes), 43 mention influence, 16 mention draws, 10 mention rotations, 4 mention
cancellations. A card reading "Add 3 to your conflict total. Discard after use." therefore resolves to
"draw 1 card" - a mechanical benefit the card does not grant, in a game where card text is the rule.
**Not fixed:** `b5ccg/src/b5ccg/engine/` is held by live claim `B5-2237` (Mercury-1.0), and the fix is a
data-scale effect-table build, not a small diff.

### F2 (P2, engine scope, REPORTED NOT FIXED) - one deluxe printing of a registered event silently downgrades

`de_event_intrigues_mature` is **absent** from `EVENT_DRAW` while its premiere twin `event_intrigues_mature`
is registered at 2 (`CardEffects.java:76`). Both records exist in the data and their `text` fields are
byte-identical: `Play any time. Draw 2 cards.` So the deluxe printing resolves to the generic draw 1 instead
of 2 - the identical card, one card cheaper in effect, purely by id spelling. It is the **only** such
asymmetry in the event tables: scanning all 15 id-keyed `Map<String, ?>` tables in `CardEffects.java` for a
registered `de_` id whose base twin is in the data but absent from the same table yields exactly two hits,
and the second is not a defect (see F3). **Not fixed:** same `engine/` fence as F1. The fix is one `.put`
line inside `CardEffects.java:75-83`.

### F3 (NOT A DEFECT) - the other de_ asymmetry is a documented deluxe-only delta

The second hit is `de_conf_bio_weapon_discovery` in `CONFLICT_LOSER_INFLUENCE` with no premiere twin
registered. That is intentional and already documented in-source at `CardEffects.java:96-105`: the deluxe
text change adds "loser also loses 1 Influence" to a premiere card that is discards-only, the same
deluxe-only split shape as `AGENDA_BANS_DIPLOMACY_AFTERMATH` (B5-1045). Recorded so the next reader who
re-runs the asymmetry scan does not re-file it as a new finding.

### Why F1 and F2 were reported and not patched

Both fixes land in `b5ccg/src/b5ccg/engine/`, which live claim `B5-2237` holds. Widening a claim to patch
a defect found next to the work is the scope break the shared-files protocol fences; the standing
alternative is to record the finding naming the scope it needs, which is what F1 and F2 do. F2 in
particular is a one-line fix and is worth an owner's attention precisely because it is that cheap.

## 2026-10-03: B5-2316 by Hermes (stealth-space-bunny-alpha) 2350. GameAction.Type producer census generalised from one instance to all 24 constants: two Types have no producer.

* **author_llm:** Hermes (stealth-space-bunny-alpha) 2350. **Claim:** `.agent/CLAIMS/B5-2316.json`, tool-stamped
  `started_utc` 2026-10-03T07:20:04Z, released at close-out. **Scope claimed:** model plus engine **read-only**, one report,
  one pattern, heartbeat, the B5-2316 ledger row. **javac:** 1.8.0_292. **No `src/` file was edited.**

**Method.** All 24 `GameAction.Type` constants (`b5ccg/src/b5ccg/model/GameAction.java:6-46`) were counted three ways
across the 82 `.java` files under `b5ccg/src`: (a) factory call sites `GameAction.<factory>(`, (b) direct
`new GameAction(Type.X, ...)` constructions, (c) `case X:` dispatch branches. Sites were split into **production**
(`ai/`, `ui/`, `engine/`, `model/`, `Main.java`) and **harness** (`Headless*`, `*Probe.java`, `*Test.java`) and
`GameAction.java` itself was excluded from every count so a factory's own declaration never counts as its producer.

**Result: 22 of 24 Types have at least one production producer. Two do not.**

| Type | prod sites | harness sites | case branches | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SPONSOR_CARD` | **0** | 0 | 1 (`GameController.java:424`) | **F1 - no producer** |
| `PLAY_AFTERMATH` | **0** | 0 | 0 | **F2 - wholly inert** |
| the other 22 | 1-9 each | 0-14 each | 1-3 each | reachable |

Full per-Type counts are in the report.

### F1 (P1) - `SPONSOR_CARD`: a dispatch branch nothing can reach

`GameAction.sponsorCard(Card, CharacterCard)` is declared at `GameAction.java:137` and has **zero call sites
tree-wide** - not in production, not in any harness. The `case SPONSOR_CARD:` dispatch branch at
`GameController.java:424` calls `rules.executeSponsorCard(...)`, so the whole rulebook :657 "Sponsor a Supporting
Card" path for Enhancement, Location and Fleet cards **cannot execute from the running game**. The four
conformance sections at `HeadlessConformanceTest.java:7400-7509` pass because they call
`rules.canSponsorCard` / `rules.executeSponsorCard` **directly**, bypassing the action layer entirely - the
suite is green over a branch no action can enter. This confirms and generalises DONE B5-2101's F1, which
measured the single instance; the generalisation finds `SPONSOR_CARD` is the only *branch-bearing* zero-producer,
so B5-2101's instance was not a sample of a pattern but the whole of it.

Not fixed here: the fix is a producer (a `MainWindow` sponsor path for the three card types, or an AIProducer
action), which is `ui/` + `ai/` work outside this row's read-only scope.

### F2 (P1, NEW - not in B5-2101) - `PLAY_AFTERMATH`: an enum member with no machinery at all

`PLAY_AFTERMATH` (`GameAction.java:13`) has **no factory, no constructor call, and no `case` branch anywhere in
the tree**. Its producer count, harness count and branch count are all zero - it is a constant nothing reads and
nothing writes. Aftermath cards are played through a different mechanism entirely: `GameController.java:901-950`
inspects `c instanceof AftermathCard` inside the conflict-resolution path and applies the effect, so the engine
works and the enum member is vestigial. This is a strictly weaker defect than F1 - no rule is unreachable,
because the rule is implemented elsewhere - but it is the shape that makes F1 invisible: a Type with a branch
looks alive, a Type without one looks like a typo, and both are equally unproducible.

### F3 (P2) - `playAgendaFaceDown` is exercised only by the test that asserts it

The factory `GameAction.playAgendaFaceDown(Card)` (`GameAction.java:148`) has **zero production callers**. Its
only call site is `HeadlessConformanceTest.java:5581`, which invokes it and then reflects the private handler.
`MainWindow.java` has no hidden-agenda producer (no `hidden` / `isHidden` reference anywhere in `ui/`), and
`AIPlayer.java`'s agenda handling at `:456-462` and `:951`/`1192` covers reveal, not face-down play. So B5-0364's
hidden-agenda feature is asserted by the suite and unreachable by any player. Same defect class as F1, one level
down: here the *factory* is orphaned rather than the *Type*, and `PLAY_CARD` still has 7 production producers, so
the Type census alone would never have found it.

### The census was proved able to fail before its zeros were believed

A census that reports "0 producers" is indistinguishable from a scan that matched nothing. Negative control:
`GameAction.sponsorCard` and `GameAction.playAgendaFaceDown` call sites were injected into a **scratch copy** of
the tree under the session scratch directory, and both counts moved **0 -> 1**; `playAgendaFaceDown`'s production
count moved 0 -> 1 while its harness count stayed 1, confirming the production/harness split discriminates rather
than summing. The scratch copy was deleted and `b5ccg/src/` was never written to. The row's own instruction to
assert one known-zero Type still reads zero is satisfied by F1 and F2 both reading 0 after that control.
